docs.title: Junction relocation and interface projection (2D)
docs.text:
Move a finished 2D mesh's junction vertices onto the junctions the mask itself gives (opt-in).

Opt-in. It is the 2D port of dw3d's junction_relocation + junction_curves: the connectivity is frozen (the edge array, hence every interface and junction identity, is never changed); only the coordinates of junction vertices move, and only when four guards accept the move.

Move a 2D mesh's interface vertices onto the mask's own interface locus (opt-in, after the junction relocation).

The 2D port of dw3d's locus projection. Connectivity is frozen: only the coordinates of interface vertices move, under the guards of :mod:dw2d.junction_relocation.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: dw2d's mesh vertices are Delaunay points chosen on the pixel lattice (integer row, column), so every junction vertex sits on a pixel centre, while a junction of the label image lies on the dual lattice: the corner shared by four pixels. On the equilibrium-foam benchmark (exact rasterisations of certified circular-arc foams with known tensions; held-out split, 159 images, min_dist 3) moving the junctions onto the mask's own junctions lowered the case angle error (per case the median over junctions of the mean absolute error of the three material-attributed angles, then the median over cases) by 1.76 deg [1.51, 1.94] from 9.15 deg, the junction position error by 0.21 px, and the gauge-matched tension error by 0.025 [0.011, 0.029] (per-junction Young-Dupre rows), on every scale tier (cell radius 10, 20, 40 px). With smooth boundary noise of 0.5 px RMS it still helps (-1.49 deg, -0.019); at 1 px it helps the angles only (-0.66 deg); at 2 px it is neutral on angles. These are measurements on synthetic masks, not a guarantee on real masks.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
• Mask junctions. A dual-lattice corner at continuous (row, col) = (i + 0.5, j + 0.5) is shared by pixels (i, j), (i, j+1), (i+1, j), (i+1, j+1). It is a junction corner of the triple (a, b, c) when its four pixels hold exactly those three labels; a corner whose four pixels hold four labels counts for each of the four triples it contains (dw3d's rule, which carries a junction into a four-fold point instead of stopping it short). Per triple, 8-connected components of junction corners are one mask junction each, located at the component's centroid.
  • Identity. Mesh junctions (vertices whose incident edges involve exactly three materials) are paired with mask junctions of the same triple by the Hungarian assignment on Euclidean distance, pairs farther than gate_px (3 px) rejected, and only for triples whose two counts agree ("matched"). A vertex of four or more materials is never moved.
  • Guards. Moves are applied one vertex at a time in ascending vertex index against the configuration as it stands. A move is accepted only if (1) no incident edge becomes shorter than MIN_EDGE_PX; (2) the number of proper crossings between non-adjacent edges does not increase — moving v changes only the edges incident to v, so the change of the whole-mesh count equals the change restricted to pairs involving those edges (an exact identity, evaluated against a candidate set that provably contains every edge that can meet them); (3) no edge incident to the moved vertex comes into a contact it was not in before the move (see "Edge contacts" below); (4) no material's signed area (dw2d Dcel.compute_areas over the oriented edges) changes sign or reaches zero. A refused move is dropped, never repaired: the vertex stays where it was. Whole-mesh recounts of crossings and of contacts before and after certify (2) and (3) globally; a rise raises.

docs.title: Edge contacts
docs.text:
Guard (2) counts proper crossings in floating point, so it lets through a move that makes two edges touch: on the equilibrium-foam benchmark at a cell radius of 40 px, the projection of :mod:dw2d.locus_projection flattened 141 Z-shaped turns of plain interface chains so that a vertex landed exactly on a non-adjacent edge (an endpoint inside another edge) and the edge before it folded back by exactly 180 degrees. Guard (3) refuses every new contact of either kind, decided exactly:

  • two edges sharing no vertex are in contact when the closed segments meet: a proper crossing, a T-touch (an endpoint of one lies on the other), coincident vertices (two distinct vertices with identical coordinates, endpoints of both), or a collinear overlap (four collinear endpoints sharing one point or a sub-segment);
  • two edges sharing one vertex s are in contact when their other endpoints lie on the same ray from s: one edge runs back along the other (an adjacent overlap, a turn of exactly 180 degrees).

A pair counts as new when it is not in contact before the move, or in contact of another class. Every coordinate is a binary64 float, hence an exact rational. Orientation signs use Shewchuk's static filter for orient2d and, when the filter cannot certify the sign, the determinant in fractions.Fraction; comparisons of coordinates are float comparisons, which are exact. On that benchmark the guard refuses 143 projection moves in 38 of the 53 meshes at 40 px and leaves 0 contacts; at 10 and 20 px, where the projection creates none, it refuses nothing and the vertices are bitwise unchanged. It keeps the Z turns of the plain mesh (two turns of opposite signs) rather than removing them.

Units and conventions: coordinates in pixels, (row, col), the frame of geometry_reconstruction_2d's vertices; the label image is the one the mesh was built from (after expansion_labels). Nothing reads ground truth. Deterministic.

Failure modes: a mesh with no matched triple is returned unchanged (planned = 0); a triple whose mesh and mask junction counts differ is left untouched and counted (unmatched_triples); the thresholds are fixed and are not tuning parameters.

docs.title: GuardedVertexMover
docs.text:
GuardedVertexMover(verts, edges)

Vertex positions over a frozen edge array, moved one vertex at a time under the four guards.

Inputs: verts (V, 2) float (copied), edges (E, 4) int [v1, v2, m1, m2]. try_move(v, p) applies the move and returns "" or the name of the refusing guard, checked in this order: "short_edge", "crossing", "contact", "area_sign". The candidate search for the crossing and contact guards is a KD-tree on the initial edge midpoints; its radius adds twice the largest displacement applied so far, which bounds both how far any midpoint has moved and how much any half-length has grown, so the candidate set always contains every edge the moved edges can meet.

docs.title: whole_mesh_contacts
docs.text:
whole_mesh_contacts(verts, edges)

Number of pairs of edges of a 2D mesh in contact, of any class (see "Edge contacts" above).

verts (V, 2) float, edges (E, >= 2) int (first two columns = vertex indices). Pairs of edges sharing no vertex count when the closed segments meet (proper crossing, T-touch, coincident vertices, collinear overlap); pairs sharing one vertex count when one runs back along the other. Zero-length edges are skipped. Candidate pairs come from a KD-tree on edge midpoints with a radius covering the two longest half-edges, then an exact bounding-box test; the classes are exact.

The 2D counterpart of dw3d.relocate_junction_vertices, with the same argument order: the mask first, then the mesh. This module's docstring says what it does, under which guards, and what it was measured to buy. dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm runs it by default (set_junction_relocation).

docs.title: Why, and why only after the junction relocation
docs.text: dw2d's vertices are pixel centres, while the label image's interface between labels a and b lies between pixel centres. On the equilibrium-foam benchmark (exact rasterisations of certified circular-arc foams with known tensions; held-out split, 159 images, min_dist 3), the projection alone made the case angle error worse (+0.46 deg [+0.19, +0.56]) and the tension error worse (+0.014), but applied after the junction relocation it lowered the angle error by 2.45 deg [2.07, 2.68] from 9.15 deg and the gauge-matched tension error by 0.029, and it stayed better than the legacy mesh with smooth boundary noise of 0.5 and 1 px RMS (-1.96 deg and -1.29 deg; tensions -0.023 and -0.021). The interaction (harmful alone, helpful composed) is measured, its mechanism is not. Hence geometry_reconstruction_2d(..., project_interface_vertices=True) requires relocate_junctions=True.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
For every vertex of exactly one interface (a, b) — degree 2, both incident edges carrying the same pair, not a junction, not on the image border — the target is the zero of psi_ab(x) = (D_a(x) - D_b(x)) / 2, D_x the Euclidean distance to the nearest pixel centre of label x (scipy.ndimage.distance_transform_edt), interpolated bilinearly. Newton steps along grad psi, at most MAX_ITERATIONS, stop at |psi| < TOLERANCE_PX; a vertex whose iteration does not converge, or would move farther than MAX_DISPLACEMENT_PX, is left in place. Moves are applied in ascending vertex index under the four guards (short edge, crossing count, edge contact, signed area); whole-mesh recounts of crossings and of contacts before and after certify the crossing and contact guards globally (a rise raises). The contact guard is the one that matters here: on the equilibrium-foam benchmark at 40 px, the projection without it flattened 141 Z-shaped turns of plain interface chains into an edge touching another and a turn of exactly 180 degrees; with it those moves are refused and the vertex stays where it was (:mod:dw2d.junction_relocation, "Edge contacts").

Units and conventions: pixels, (row, col), the frame of geometry_reconstruction_2d's vertices; the label image the mesh was built from (after expansion_labels). Nothing reads ground truth; deterministic. Cost: one distance transform per label present.

docs.title: Masks from meshes (2D)
docs.text:
Rebuild an approximate label image from a compressed segmentation (a 2-D mesh, its seeds and the image shape).

The rebuild draws every mesh edge into a pixel mask (Bresenham's line between the two ends, each rounded to the nearest pixel centre), then grows one region per seed by a watershed on the distance to the drawn lines. It is an approximation: measured on one shipped mask, 95.6 % of the pixels agree with the mask the mesh was built from. dw3d's rebuild of a 3-D mask is exact; dw2d's is not, yet.

The names mirror dw3d's: reconstruct_mask_from_dict(dictionary) and reconstruct_mask_from_saved_file_dict(filename).

docs.title: Reconstruction algorithms (2D)
docs.text:
Build dw2d's mesh reconstruction algorithm, step by step or at its defaults, with dw3d's names.

dw3d's factory chooses among several EDTs, point placements, tesselations and face scores; dw2d has one of each, so its factory keeps the setters that have a 2D meaning (set_peak_local_points_placement_method, set_junction_relocation, set_canonical_triangle_order) and adds the 2D-only options as setters (set_interface_projection, set_pinch_vertex_repair, set_near_tie_sliver_relabelling, set_label_expansion, set_score_samples).

dw2d's mesh reconstruction algorithm, with the names, arguments and return layout of dw3d's.

Configure, then run: dw2d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm or dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory build a MeshReconstructionAlgorithm; construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask) runs it and returns (points, segments, labels); one object can mesh several masks, each reconstruction replacing the last mesh and every report about it. The computation is dw2d's (the engine behind the deprecated geometry_reconstruction_2d), unchanged: the same mask and options give the same arrays, bit for bit.

Conventions, stated once here and in dw3d's package docstring:

  • The mask is a 2-D integer array; label 0 is the medium, every other label a cell. points are in the mask's index order, (row, column), in pixels: the centre of pixel (i, j) is the point (i, j).
  • labels[n] = (a, b) with a < b are the two materials edge n separates. Orientation, dw3d's rule in index order (since 0.8.0): each edge is the positively oriented boundary of a. Material a lies on the left of points[segments[n, 0]] -> points[segments[n, 1]] in the (row, column) frame, so the edges of each material, taken as stored where it is a and reversed where it is b, run counter-clockwise around it in (row, column), and the edge's normal (dc, -dr) points out of a into b, as a dw3d triangle's right-hand normal does. See the user guide's page on orientation, which states the rule and the test that decides it. Until 0.8.0 each edge was stored the other way round; only the order of the two vertices within each edge changed.
  • min_distance counts pixels; its default is 4 (dw3d's is 3 voxels).

docs.title: set_canonical_triangle_order
docs.text:
set_canonical_triangle_order(enabled: bool = True) -> Self

Make the triangulation and the watershed's tie order independent of the machine (on by default).

Qhull's triangulation of the integer points is not unique where four or more are cocircular, and Qhull resolves those cells differently on different machines; with this option such cells are re-triangulated by a fixed rule and triangles, dual-graph edges and equal scores are taken in canonical order. False is dw2d 0.1.5's route (named deterministic=False before 0.8.0). dw3d's analogue is canonical_tetrahedron_order.

docs.title: MeshReconstructionAlgorithm
docs.text:
MeshReconstructionAlgorithm(print_info: bool = False, min_distance: int = DEFAULT_MIN_DISTANCE, *, relocate_junctions: bool = True, canonical_triangle_order: bool = True, interface_projection: bool = False, pinch_vertex_repair: bool = True, near_tie_sliver_relabelling: bool | None = None, label_expansion: int = 0, score_samples: int = 10, pad_thin_medium_margins: bool = True)

Algorithm that builds a 2-D multimaterial polyline mesh from a 2-D segmentation mask.

Build one with dw2d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm or dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory. The mesh is (points, segments, labels): points (n, 2) float64 in the mask's (row, column) order, in pixels unless built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units; segments (m, 2) int64 vertex indices; labels (m, 2) int64, the two materials each edge separates, smaller first (orientation: the module docstring).

Attributes:

Name Type Description print_info bool

whether to print the size of the triangulation's dual graph.

min_distance int

the point placement's minimum distance between points, in pixels.

relocate_junctions bool

move junction vertices onto the mask's own junctions after meshing (default True).

canonical_triangle_order bool

a machine-independent triangulation and tie order (default True; dw3d's analogue is canonical_tetrahedron_order).

interface_projection bool

project interface vertices onto the mask's interface locus (default False; requires relocate_junctions).

pinch_vertex_repair bool

absorb label fragments and repair pinch vertices after the watershed (default True).

near_tie_sliver_relabelling bool | None

relabel near-tie slivers (default None: on without relocation, off with it).

label_expansion int

grow the labels by this many pixels before meshing (skimage.segmentation.expand_labels; default 0), for masks whose cells do not touch.

score_samples int

points sampled along each triangle edge to score it (default 10).

pad_thin_medium_margins bool

mesh the mask padded with label 0 on every side of the image that no cell reaches and whose margin is below 2 * min_distance + 2 pixels, up to that margin, and return the mesh in the mask's frame (default True since 0.8.0; False gives the meshes of earlier versions). A mask whose cells reach every side or stay that far from it is meshed as before, bit for bit. See dw2d.thin_medium_margins; medium_margin_padding says which sides were padded.

Set the options; see the class docstring. Every option is also an attribute that can be set before a run.

The label-0 padding the last reconstruction added to the mask's sides, in pixels, by side name.

Empty when the mask was meshed as given (the common case); None before any reconstruction. See pad_thin_medium_margins and dw2d.thin_medium_margins.

docs.title: image_border_vertices property
docs.text:
image_border_vertices: NDArray[int64]

The indices of the mesh vertices on the image border, sorted.

Taken from the triangulation's structure (the endpoints of its hull edges) before any vertex moves; the junction relocation and the projection never move them. foambryo's 2D inference excludes the junctions there, where a cell-cell interface meets the image border at a straight 180-degree wedge that is not a contact angle.

docs.title: cut_cells property
docs.text:
cut_cells: tuple[int, ...]

The cells (non-zero labels) with a vertex on the image border: cells the image cuts, ascending.

dw3d's cut_cells names the cells with a crop face; in 2D a cell is cut where its boundary reaches the image border. Their pressures are not withheld by foambryo in 2D: Laplace's law reads them from the interfaces inside the image.

Keys: points, segments, labels, seeds (one pixel index per label of the mask, in ascending label order), image_shape and image_border_vertices. dw2d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict turns it back into an approximate mask; it expects the points in pixels, so read this before any scaling (after construct_mesh_in_physical_units, divide the points by the pixel size first).

docs.text:
construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmented_image: NDArray[integer]) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int64], NDArray[np.int64]]

Build a 2-D mesh from a segmentation mask.

After the call, last_constructed_mesh, image_border_vertices, cut_cells, relocation_report, interface_projection_report, unresolved_cells and enclosed_medium_pockets describe this mesh, and save_to_rec_mesh writes no physical frame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmented_image NDArray[integer]

the 2-D integer label mask; label 0 is the medium, every other label a cell.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description tuple tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[int64], NDArray[int64]]

(points, segments, labels): (n, 2) float64 in pixels, (row, column); (m, 2) int64; (m, 2) int64 (smaller label first).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for a mask that is not 2-D (see checked_two_dimensional_mask), or for interface_projection without relocate_junctions.

Warns:

Type Description UserWarning

for a mask whose dtype is not an integer type.

EnclosedMediumWarning

once, when a piece of label 0 touches no side of the image (it is meshed as the outer medium), naming each such pocket.

UnresolvedCellWarning

once, when a label of the mask is absent from the mesh, naming each. Since 0.8.0 this includes a mask whose mesh has no edge at all (returned empty, (0, 2) segments); before, it raised IndexError.

ThinMediumMarginWarning

once, when a cell's edges lie on a side of the image its pixels do not reach and that could not be padded (see pad_thin_medium_margins), naming each such cell, the side and its margin.

A mask with a side that no cell reaches and whose margin is below 2 * min_distance + 2 pixels is meshed padded with label 0 on such sides (pad_thin_medium_margins, medium_margin_padding); the mesh and the compressed segmentation are in the mask's frame either way.

docs.title: construct_mesh_in_physical_units
docs.text:
construct_mesh_in_physical_units(segmented_image: NDArray[integer], spacing: tuple[float, float], *, spacing_unit: str | None = None, axis_order: str = 'yx') -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int64], NDArray[np.int64]]

Build a mesh in physical units from a mask of square pixels.

The mask is meshed on its own pixel grid (construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, min_distance in pixels), and the points are multiplied by the pixel size: a point at pixel index i is at i * h, so the centre of the first pixel is the origin. Only square pixels are accepted in 0.8.0 (dw3d resamples anisotropic voxels to cubic ones; the accuracy of the same route in 2D has not been measured).

After this call save_to_rec_mesh records coordinate_frame = physical, axis_order, spacing, spacing_unit (when given) and source_shape in the file's appendix. Any later reconstruction clears them.

the 2-D integer label mask.

required spacing tuple[float, float]

the pixel size along the mask's axes 0 and 1, (dy, dx); the two must be equal (relative tolerance 1e-6).

required spacing_unit str | None

the unit of spacing (e.g. "um"), recorded, not used.

None axis_order str

what the mask's axes are, recorded, not used. Defaults to "yx".

'yx'

(points, segments, labels) as construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask returns them, the points in the unit of spacing. For a spacing of (1, 1) they are bitwise the pixel ones.

docs.title: Reports and warnings (2D)
docs.text:
What dw2d's reconstruction did and what it found, as frozen records and warning classes.

The names follow dw3d's where the concept is the same (JunctionRelocationReport, EnclosedMediumWarning, UnresolvedCellWarning). The warning classes are dw2d's own, distinct from dw3d's classes of the same names: neither package imports the other at module level, so a filter on dw3d.EnclosedMediumWarning does not catch dw2d's (filter on both, or on their base class UserWarning).

docs.title: EnclosedMediumWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A pocket of label 0 enclosed by cells (it touches no side of the image) is meshed as the outer medium.

dw2d has no enclosed-medium region yet (dw3d labels such a pocket as its own medium region): the pocket's triangles take label 0, so the mesh treats it as contact with the outer medium. The warning names each pocket.

docs.title: UnresolvedCellWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A label of the mask is absent from the finished mesh: the reconstruction did not resolve that cell.

Usually a cell narrower than the point placement's min_distance, which no triangle of the watershed reached. The warning names each such label; MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.unresolved_cells lists them.

docs.title: ThinMediumMarginWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A cell's edges lie on a side of the image that its pixels do not reach, and padding could not prevent it.

Emitted once per reconstruction, naming each such cell, the side, the cell's medium margin to it and why the side was not padded: a cell reaches it (it is a crop), padding is switched off, or the margin is already thin_margin_bound(min_distance) or more. The cell may have taken some of the medium between it and the side. The same name and meaning as dw3d's warning; see dw2d.thin_medium_margins.

docs.title: Thin margins of medium (2D)
docs.text:
A thin margin of medium between a cell and the image border: why the cell took it, and the padding that prevents it.

The same defect as in dw3d (dw3d.thin_medium_margins), and the same rule.

docs.title: The defect
docs.text: dw2d's distance field is 0 on the image's outer ring of pixels (dw2d.Geometric_utilities.pad_mask makes the image border a boundary), at or below the level of the membranes, and a membrane point is placed only where no lower value lies within min_distance (skimage.feature.peak_local_max). So the membrane between a cell and a side of the image a few pixels away loses its points, the triangles joining the cell's interior to the border span the medium, and the watershed gives them to the cell. Measured before 0.8.0 on single squares (side 12, 20, 32 px), squares with the margin on one side, a doublet of 20-px squares and disks (radius 10 and 16 px), at min_distance 3, 4 and 5: at margins of 2 px up to about min_distance, the membrane facing the near side carried no point, the cell had edges on a side its pixels do not reach, and its area was 1.04 to 1.73 times its pixel count; from min_distance + 1 or + 2 px on, every cell was back at 0.84 to 0.99 (its value at a margin of 16 px).

docs.title: The fix
docs.text:
dw2d places its points on the field without a random dither, so the mask can be padded before it is meshed: every side of the image that no cell reaches and whose margin (its smallest gap to a cell) is below thin_margin_bound(min_distance), 2 * min_distance + 2 as in dw3d, is padded with label 0 up to that bound, and the mesh is translated back into the mask's frame. The pixels of the mask keep the field and the points they have unpadded, except within the padded sides' reach. A mask whose cells reach every side or stay at least that far from it is meshed exactly as before. A side that a cell reaches is a crop and is never padded. A cell left with edges on a side its pixels do not reach is named by ThinMediumMarginWarning. On a padded side the mesh is that of the same tissue imaged with a wider margin, so a cell's boundary may reach past the image border there, by at most the padding.

dw3d decides from a first mesh (a vertex on a face no cell reaches), because its meshes cost more and its dither makes a padded mesh a new draw. In 2D that test would miss the defect twice over: at a margin of min_distance the cell took the medium without reaching the side (1.28 times its pixels at min_distance 4, its nearest vertex 2.5 px beyond the membrane), and a 12-px square 3 or 4 px from one side collapsed to a triangle of 0.23 times its pixels, with no vertex near the side, at min_distance 5 (0.84 at a margin of 12 px).

docs.title: The dw2d package
docs.text:
The names dw2d exports (dw2d.__all__). The names of dw2d 0.1.5 that are not listed here still resolve through 0.8.x, with a DeprecationWarning (see migrating from dw2d 0.1.5).

If you use dw2d, please cite: Yamamoto K., Ichbiah S., Perez M., Borrego-Pinto J., Delbary F., Goehring N. W., Northrop P., Turlier H., Charras G. Spatiotemporal mapping of the contractile and adhesive forces sculpting early C. elegans embryos. Developmental Cell 61(6), 1273–1288.e4 (2026), doi:10.1016/j.devcel.2026.04.013.

Delaunay-Watershed 2D (dw2d): build a multimaterial polyline mesh from a 2-D segmentation mask.

The top-level names mirror dw3d's (get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm, MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory, MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, save_to_rec_mesh, the compressed segmentation, reconstruct_mask_from_dict), so that dw2d is used exactly like dw3d; dw3d's algorithm also hands a 2-D mask to dw2d.

Conventions used everywhere in the package:

  • The mask is a 2-D integer array; label 0 is the medium, every other label a cell.
  • A mesh is (points, segments, labels): points (n, 2) float64 in the mask's index order (row, column), in pixels (the centre of pixel (i, j) is the point (i, j)); segments (m, 2) int64 vertex indices; labels (m, 2) int64, the two materials each edge separates, smaller first.
  • Orientation, one rule with dw3d's (since 0.8.0): each edge is the positively oriented boundary of its first label in the index frame. Material labels[n, 0] lies on the left of segments[n, 0] -> segments[n, 1] in (row, column), so the normal (dc, -dr) of the edge (its tangent (dr, dc) turned clockwise) points out of labels[n, 0] and into labels[n, 1], as a dw3d triangle's right-hand normal does. A cell alone in the medium therefore has a negative signed area, as it has a negative signed volume in 3D (the user guide's page on orientation). Until 0.8.0 each edge was stored the other way round.
  • min_distance counts pixels and defaults to 4 (dw3d: 3 voxels).

Names that dw2d 0.1.5 exported and that are not listed in __all__ (geometry_reconstruction_2d, the .rec functions write_mesh_bin, read_rec_file_bin, ..., the half-edge and plotting helpers of dw2d.Dcel) still work through 0.8.x with a DeprecationWarning naming their replacement or their module, and will be removed in 0.9. The third-party names 0.1.5 leaked by its star imports (dw2d.np, dw2d.plt, dw2d.pickle, ...) are gone.

docs.title: DCEL_Data
docs.text:
DCEL_Data(Verts, Edges, allow_several_loops=False, image_border_vertices=None)

DCEL Graph containing faces, half-edges and vertices.

Half-edge structure of a 2D multimaterial mesh.

allow_several_loops (default False): see create_halfedges_from_edges; when True, a material may have several boundary loops (one Face per loop, same key).

image_border_vertices (default None): the indices of the vertices on the image border, kept as self.image_border_vertices (a sorted int64 array, or None when not given). return_dcel passes the mark geometry_reconstruction_2d takes from the triangulation's structure (image_border_vertices), before any vertex moves; foambryo's 2D inference reads it to exclude the junctions on the border.

docs.title: MeshReconstructionAlgorithm
docs.text:
MeshReconstructionAlgorithm(print_info: bool = False, min_distance: int = DEFAULT_MIN_DISTANCE, *, relocate_junctions: bool = True, canonical_triangle_order: bool = True, interface_projection: bool = False, pinch_vertex_repair: bool = True, near_tie_sliver_relabelling: bool | None = None, label_expansion: int = 0, score_samples: int = 10, pad_thin_medium_margins: bool = True)

Algorithm that builds a 2-D multimaterial polyline mesh from a 2-D segmentation mask.

Build one with dw2d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm or dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory. The mesh is (points, segments, labels): points (n, 2) float64 in the mask's (row, column) order, in pixels unless built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units; segments (m, 2) int64 vertex indices; labels (m, 2) int64, the two materials each edge separates, smaller first (orientation: the module docstring).

Attributes:

Name Type Description print_info bool

whether to print the size of the triangulation's dual graph.

min_distance int

the point placement's minimum distance between points, in pixels.

relocate_junctions bool

move junction vertices onto the mask's own junctions after meshing (default True).

canonical_triangle_order bool

a machine-independent triangulation and tie order (default True; dw3d's analogue is canonical_tetrahedron_order).

interface_projection bool

project interface vertices onto the mask's interface locus (default False; requires relocate_junctions).

pinch_vertex_repair bool

absorb label fragments and repair pinch vertices after the watershed (default True).

near_tie_sliver_relabelling bool | None

relabel near-tie slivers (default None: on without relocation, off with it).

label_expansion int

grow the labels by this many pixels before meshing (skimage.segmentation.expand_labels; default 0), for masks whose cells do not touch.

score_samples int

points sampled along each triangle edge to score it (default 10).

pad_thin_medium_margins bool

mesh the mask padded with label 0 on every side of the image that no cell reaches and whose margin is below 2 * min_distance + 2 pixels, up to that margin, and return the mesh in the mask's frame (default True since 0.8.0; False gives the meshes of earlier versions). A mask whose cells reach every side or stay that far from it is meshed as before, bit for bit. See dw2d.thin_medium_margins; medium_margin_padding says which sides were padded.

Set the options; see the class docstring. Every option is also an attribute that can be set before a run.

docs.title: medium_margin_padding property
docs.text:
medium_margin_padding: dict[str, int] | None

The label-0 padding the last reconstruction added to the mask's sides, in pixels, by side name.

Empty when the mask was meshed as given (the common case); None before any reconstruction. See pad_thin_medium_margins and dw2d.thin_medium_margins.

docs.title: last_constructed_mesh property
docs.text:

The last mesh built, (points, segments, labels). The algorithm's own arrays, not copies.

docs.title: image_border_vertices property
docs.text:
image_border_vertices: NDArray[int64]

The indices of the mesh vertices on the image border, sorted.

Taken from the triangulation's structure (the endpoints of its hull edges) before any vertex moves; the junction relocation and the projection never move them. foambryo's 2D inference excludes the junctions there, where a cell-cell interface meets the image border at a straight 180-degree wedge that is not a contact angle.

docs.title: cut_cells property
docs.text:
cut_cells: tuple[int, ...]

The cells (non-zero labels) with a vertex on the image border: cells the image cuts, ascending.

dw3d's cut_cells names the cells with a crop face; in 2D a cell is cut where its boundary reaches the image border. Their pressures are not withheld by foambryo in 2D: Laplace's law reads them from the interfaces inside the image.

The labels that are a medium: (0,) (dw2d has no enclosed-medium region).

The last mesh as dw2d's half-edge structure, dw2d.DCEL_Data, which measures angles, lengths, areas and curvatures; it carries image_border_vertices. Built from the points as they are now (physical if scaled).

docs.title: last_compressed_segmentation property
docs.text:
last_compressed_segmentation: dict[str, Any]

The last mesh, the watershed seeds and the mask's shape, as a dictionary.

Keys: points, segments, labels, seeds (one pixel index per label of the mask, in ascending label order), image_shape and image_border_vertices. dw2d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict turns it back into an approximate mask; it expects the points in pixels, so read this before any scaling (after construct_mesh_in_physical_units, divide the points by the pixel size first).

docs.title: construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask
docs.text:
construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmented_image: NDArray[integer]) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int64], NDArray[np.int64]]

Build a 2-D mesh from a segmentation mask.

After the call, last_constructed_mesh, image_border_vertices, cut_cells, relocation_report, interface_projection_report, unresolved_cells and enclosed_medium_pockets describe this mesh, and save_to_rec_mesh writes no physical frame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmented_image NDArray[integer]

the 2-D integer label mask; label 0 is the medium, every other label a cell.

required

Returns:

Name Type Description tuple tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[int64], NDArray[int64]]

(points, segments, labels): (n, 2) float64 in pixels, (row, column); (m, 2) int64; (m, 2) int64 (smaller label first).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for a mask that is not 2-D (see checked_two_dimensional_mask), or for interface_projection without relocate_junctions.

Warns:

Type Description UserWarning

for a mask whose dtype is not an integer type.

EnclosedMediumWarning

once, when a piece of label 0 touches no side of the image (it is meshed as the outer medium), naming each such pocket.

UnresolvedCellWarning

once, when a label of the mask is absent from the mesh, naming each. Since 0.8.0 this includes a mask whose mesh has no edge at all (returned empty, (0, 2) segments); before, it raised IndexError.

ThinMediumMarginWarning

once, when a cell's edges lie on a side of the image its pixels do not reach and that could not be padded (see pad_thin_medium_margins), naming each such cell, the side and its margin.

A mask with a side that no cell reaches and whose margin is below 2 * min_distance + 2 pixels is meshed padded with label 0 on such sides (pad_thin_medium_margins, medium_margin_padding); the mesh and the compressed segmentation are in the mask's frame either way.

docs.title: construct_mesh_in_physical_units
docs.text:
construct_mesh_in_physical_units(segmented_image: NDArray[integer], spacing: tuple[float, float], *, spacing_unit: str | None = None, axis_order: str = 'yx') -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.int64], NDArray[np.int64]]

Build a mesh in physical units from a mask of square pixels.

The mask is meshed on its own pixel grid (construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, min_distance in pixels), and the points are multiplied by the pixel size: a point at pixel index i is at i * h, so the centre of the first pixel is the origin. Only square pixels are accepted in 0.8.0 (dw3d resamples anisotropic voxels to cubic ones; the accuracy of the same route in 2D has not been measured).

After this call save_to_rec_mesh records coordinate_frame = physical, axis_order, spacing, spacing_unit (when given) and source_shape in the file's appendix. Any later reconstruction clears them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmented_image NDArray[integer]

the 2-D integer label mask.

required spacing tuple[float, float]

the pixel size along the mask's axes 0 and 1, (dy, dx); the two must be equal (relative tolerance 1e-6).

required spacing_unit str | None

the unit of spacing (e.g. "um"), recorded, not used.

None axis_order str

what the mask's axes are, recorded, not used. Defaults to "yx".

'yx'

Returns:

Name Type Description tuple tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[int64], NDArray[int64]]

(points, segments, labels) as construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask returns them, the points in the unit of spacing. For a spacing of (1, 1) they are bitwise the pixel ones.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for a spacing that is not two positive finite numbers, or whose two values differ.

docs.title: set_canonical_triangle_order
docs.text:
set_canonical_triangle_order(enabled: bool = True) -> Self

Make the triangulation and the watershed's tie order independent of the machine (on by default).

Qhull's triangulation of the integer points is not unique where four or more are cocircular, and Qhull resolves those cells differently on different machines; with this option such cells are re-triangulated by a fixed rule and triangles, dual-graph edges and equal scores are taken in canonical order. False is dw2d 0.1.5's route (named deterministic=False before 0.8.0). dw3d's analogue is canonical_tetrahedron_order.

docs.title: Enclosed media
docs.text: Pockets of medium that the tissue encloses: their own regions, flagged as media, instead of part of a cell.

docs.title: Why this exists
docs.text: The watershed places one seed per label value, at the label's largest EDT value. The medium, label 0, is one value, so before 0.7.1 it had one seed, in whichever of its pieces was deepest. An enclosed pocket of label 0 (a lumen, a cavity) had none: its tetrahedra formed one unseeded group, which the first seeded cell it reached took whole. On a 697-cell embryo with a 389 918-voxel lumen, one lining cell came out at 2.40 times its voxel volume, and no lining cell kept a membrane against the lumen. When a pocket was deeper than the exterior (a tight crop), label 0's seed fell in the pocket and the exterior was absorbed instead.

docs.title: What it does
docs.text:
Pieces of label 0 are 6-connected (two voxels sharing a face), as foambryo's mask report counts them. A piece touching no face of the array is an enclosed pocket. A pocket becomes its own region, flagged as a medium, when its inscribed radius is at least min_distance + 1 voxels and at least two cells line it:

  • the inscribed radius is the largest Euclidean distance, in voxels, from a pocket voxel to the nearest voxel outside the pocket. Below about 3 voxels at min_distance 3 a pocket holds no tetrahedron, and a seed placed in it would take a neighbouring cell's tetrahedron instead, so it is left as before;
  • a pocket lined by one cell is a hole in that cell's segmentation, not a lumen between cells: as its own region it would be a closed surface with no triple line, whose tension no method can infer. It is left as before.

The new labels are max + 1, max + 2, ..., in the order of each pocket's lowest raster (C-order) index. Pockets left as before are reported, and EnclosedMediumWarning names the cell that took each.

Every piece of label 0 that touches the image box is exterior and gets its own label-0 seed (see dw3d.reconstruction_algorithm). A mask with no pocket at or above the bound and one exterior piece is reconstructed bitwise as before.

Herve Turlier's group, 2026.

docs.title: UnresolvedCellWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Some regions of the mask are absent from the mesh.

Emitted once per reconstruction whose finished mesh lacks a label of the mask that was meshed, whatever the cause, naming each such region with its voxel count, the cause and the min_distance; the regions are the reconstruction's enclosed_medium_report.unresolved. A smaller min_distance may mesh them. The causes:

  • no tetrahedron centroid lies in the region's voxels (a cell a few voxels thick, or smaller than the point placement's min_distance). A region's watershed seed is the tetrahedron whose centroid is nearest to its deepest voxel; here that tetrahedron belongs to a neighbour, and before 0.7.1 the region grew from it inside the neighbour, as a phantom. Since 0.7.1 the seed is dropped.
  • the region was seeded, but the watershed left it few tetrahedra (often only its seed: the rest of the region, grouped without the seed, went to a neighbour) and mesh surgery relabelled those. Since 0.8.0 such a region is named too; before, only CellVolumeDisagreementWarning listed it, as a cell absent from the mesh.
  • the region had no watershed seed (label 0 when no piece of it touches the image box), or holds tetrahedra but no triangle of the finished mesh.

docs.title: EnclosedMediumWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Enclosed pockets of medium were left to the cells around them.

Emitted once per reconstruction that leaves at least one pocket of label 0 to the cells (below the size bound, or lined by one cell). The pockets are the reconstruction's enclosed_medium_report.pockets_left_to_cells. A subclass of :class:UserWarning, so it can be silenced or promoted to an error on its own with :func:warnings.filterwarnings.

docs.title: Files
docs.text:
Read and write dw3d meshes: the .rec format with its metadata appendix, and .vtk/.vtu through meshio.

A mesh is (points, triangles, labels): (n, 3) points, (m, 3) vertex indices and (m, 2) labels, the two regions each triangle separates (label 0 is the medium). The files store the points as given: these functions neither scale nor reorder their columns. A file therefore keeps the mask's order, (z, y, x) for a microscope stack; a program that reads its columns as (x, y, z), as ParaView, MeshLab and other VTK readers do, shows the mirror image of the tissue, unless it exchanges columns 0 and 2 (and two corners of every triangle, so that each still faces the same side), as dw3d.viewing.plot_cells_polyscope does for what it draws.

The .rec reader and writer are iorec's (iorec.load_rec, iorec.save_rec, iorec.load_rec_appendix); this module keeps dw3d's names and signatures, types dw3d's own appendix keys when it reads a version-1 appendix, and writes the appendix in version 1 (see APPENDIX_VERSION_WRITTEN). Matthieu Perez 2024

rec_dimension(filename: str | Path) -> int

Whether a .rec/.arec file holds a 2-D mesh (segments) or a 3-D mesh (triangles).

The .rec format carries no dimension marker. Since 0.8.0 both packages' algorithms record dimension in the metadata appendix (dw2d always, dw3d whenever it writes an appendix); when the key is present it decides. Otherwise the layout does: in a text file, the number of coordinates on the point rows; in a binary file, which of the two layouts accounts exactly for the geometry's bytes before the appendix (_layouts_of_a_binary_rec). A file both layouts would fit (possible in principle for a binary file, never observed) is refused rather than guessed.

required

2 or 3.

if the file does not exist.

write_rec_appendix(metadata: dict[str, Any], *, written_by: str) -> bytes

Build the trailing .rec/.arec metadata appendix block.

The block is a sequence of ASCII #-prefixed key = value lines (appendix version 1, APPENDIX_VERSION_WRITTEN), headed by the rec-appendix 1 line, built by iorec.write_rec_appendix. It must be appended at the very end of the file: a trailing # block is invisible to every reader that predates it (both text and binary mode), since those readers read a count and then np.fromfile(..., count=n), which stops exactly there. required

docs.title: save_rec

save_rec(filename: str | Path, points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], binary_mode: bool = False, metadata: dict[str, Any] | None = None, crop_faces: NDArray[bool_] | None = None) -> None

Save a rec mesh file at filename. Binary or text mode are available.

Binary mode is more compact but might not be universally understood. Its layout, little-endian on every machine (iorec's), is: the number of points (uint64); the points, 3 float64 each; the number of triangles (uint64); per triangle, its 3 vertex indices (int64) then its 2 labels (int32). The points are always written as float64, the dtype load_rec reads, whatever their dtype in memory (before 0.7.0 they were written in their own dtype, so float32 points did not read back). The text layout is the point count, one line of 3 coordinates per point (each the shortest text that reads back to the same float64), the triangle count, and one v0 v1 v2 label1 label2 line per triangle. Either layout may be followed by the metadata appendix (version 1, APPENDIX_VERSION_WRITTEN). The file is written by iorec.save_rec.

Name Type Description Default filename str | Path

where to save the mesh file.

required points NDArray[float64]

(n, 3) mesh points, written as given.

required triangles NDArray[int64]

(m, 3) mesh triangles (topology).

required labels NDArray[int64]

(m, 2) the two regions each triangle separates.

required binary_mode bool

Choose binary mode. Defaults to False.

False metadata dict[str, Any] | None

appendix fields (coordinate_frame, axis_order, spacing, spacing_unit, source_shape, crop_offset, ...). Defaults to None, which writes nothing extra -- byte-for-byte the same file as before this option existed. When supplied, a trailing metadata appendix is appended after the geometry data; see write_rec_appendix.

None crop_faces NDArray[bool_] | None

(n_triangles,), True on the crop faces (see dw3d.crop_faces). When given, the crop faces are written as the last block of triangle rows (the other rows first, both blocks in their original order) and the appendix records crop_faces = <first row> <count> (<count> may be 0), so the file's rows are in a different order from the arrays passed in. A reader that ignores the appendix still reads a valid mesh, in which the crop faces look like contact with the medium; load_rec_with_crop_faces reads them back. Defaults to None, which writes the file as before this option existed.

None

if crop_faces is not a boolean array with one entry per triangle.

docs.title: Junction curves
docs.text: Trijunction curves read from the label mask and keyed to a reconstructed mesh's own junctions.

docs.title: What this is
docs.text:
extract_junction_curves returns one polyline per material triple (a, b, c), computed from the segmentation mask, and says for each whether the reconstructed mesh has exactly one trijunction of that same triple. The curves are more accurate than the mesh's own junction lines and less complete than them; both halves are measured, and the API keeps them apart so a caller cannot get one while thinking it got the other.

Nothing in the reconstruction pipeline calls this and no default changes. It is an additional read of the same mask the mesh was built from.

docs.title: Where the criterion comes from
docs.text: A dual-lattice point -- the corner shared by eight voxels -- lies on the junction line of (a, b, c) iff those eight voxels contain all three labels. junctions.junction_strata already computes exactly this predicate (|L| == 3) for point placement; what this module adds is the split by material triple, the attribution of points carrying four or more labels to every triple they contain (which carries a line into its quadruple point rather than stopping a lattice step short), and the reduction of each 26-connected component to one ordered polyline by the minimum spanning tree's diameter path. Label 0 is an ordinary material: the outer medium's contact lines with the cells are genuine trijunctions.

docs.title: The measured advantage, and the measured limitation
docs.text:
These curves were measured against a registered reference mesh on the 47-case synthetic benchmark, reading each variant at its own median junction-edge spacing so that the comparison is not a comparison of reading resolutions. The position error below is the median distance in voxels from a curve's vertices to the reference polyline; lower is better.

dw3d min_distance these curves the mesh's own lines advantage 3 0.5796 0.6735 1.16x 4 0.6146 0.7449 1.21x

(42 equilibrium cases, the default reconstruction with junction relocation, dw3d 0.7.1; on 0.7.0 without relocation the mesh's own lines sit at 0.8642 and 0.9277, and the advantage is 1.48x and 1.52x.) Of the 24 paired comparisons of BENCHMARKS.md -- two spacings, two estimators, six geometric metrics -- the 16 on tangent and position error favour the curves on at least 9,999 of 10,000 case-level bootstrap draws. At min_distance = 3, relative to the value the reference line itself scores when subsampled at the same spacing, the curves read tortuosity at 1.001 (the mesh's own lines: 1.002), curvature at 1.018 (1.024) and tangent error at 1.99x (3.35x).

They are better geometry, not correct geometry. The mask's own identifiability floor -- the best any mask-based method can do -- is 0.107 voxels (BENCHMARKS.md, "Junction curves"). These curves sit at 0.5796, a factor of 5.4 above it, and that gap is open.

docs.title: Coordinates
docs.text: Everything is in mask voxel units. A dual-lattice point (i, j, k) is emitted at (i + 0.5, j + 0.5, k + 0.5), in the frame a reconstructed dw3d mesh's points live in (construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask; not a mesh scaled by set_pixel_size or built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units). extract_junction_curves checks that the mesh it is given lies inside the mask's extent (no coordinate below -1 or above the mask's size along its axis) and refuses otherwise, because a permuted axis order would put every curve tens of voxels away and the result would silently measure the permutation. The check sees only the extent: a mesh scaled down into it, or permuted on a mask whose sides are nearly equal, passes it.

docs.title: Provenance
docs.text: The detection, the MST-diameter spine and the endpoint-preserving three-point filter, the per-case reading spacing, the identity rule against the mesh's own trijunctions and the consistency test were developed and validated on the benchmark (BENCHMARKS.md, "Junction curves"). The sub-voxel estimator lives in junction_curve_estimator.

matched is the set a caller wanting usable geometry wants: on the benchmark at min_distance = 3 its 621 curves were measured a median 0.523 voxels from all three of their own interfaces at once, with a p99 of 4.43. docs.title: extract_junction_curves
docs.text:
extract_junction_curves(segmented_mask: NDArray[uint], points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], *, estimator: Estimator = 'plain') -> JunctionCurves

Trijunction curves from the mask, keyed to the mesh's own trijunctions.

The one line a user writes::

curves = extract_junction_curves(mask, *load_rec("000_mesh.rec"))

curves.matched is the usable set. Every one of its members has exactly one counterpart among the mesh's own trijunctions of the same material triple, so it can be joined to the interfaces and the dihedral angles the reconstruction already reports. curves.invented is everything the mask says is a junction and the mesh does not have; none of 27 of those were measured within one voxel of all three of their interfaces, against a median of 0.524 voxels for the matched ones, so they are kept apart rather than merged. curves.fragmented holds real trijunctions the mask resolves as several pieces.

Reading spacing is not a parameter: the polylines are resampled at the mesh's own median trijunction-edge length, so accuracy is compared at the resolution the mesh states its lines at rather than at whatever resolution the lattice happens to give.

Cost, and why "plain" is the default. "plain" is detection only -- no linear program -- and costs about 0.8 s per benchmark case against the 1.49 s dw3d spends reconstructing that case. "anchor" solves one small linear program per returned vertex and costs roughly fifteen times as much, about eight times the whole reconstruction it annotates, and buys 9-11 % of the position error. Nobody meshing a large tissue should pay that by default, so they do not.

"anchor"'s real argument is not that 9 %: it is that the polytope's deepest interior point carries only the irreducible narrow-wedge term (a) of the mask's identifiability floor, where the detected position and the centroid both carry more. Reach for it when a systematic bias against narrow wedges would corrupt what you are inferring, not to shave a tenth of a voxel. "centroid" is kept for comparison only: it was measured carrying (a) + (b), so it is the larger systematic, not the smaller one, and it costs about thirty times the anchor's linear programs on top.

the label image the mesh was reconstructed from.

triangle vertex indices, (m, 3).

the two materials each triangle separates, (m, 2).

"plain" (default, no linear program), "anchor" or "centroid". See the cost paragraph above before changing it.

'plain'

if estimator is not one of the three, or if the mesh's coordinates do not lie inside the mask's extent.

docs.title: Junction relocation
docs.text: Move a finished mesh's trijunction vertices onto the trijunction curves the mask itself gives.

docs.title: What it does, and what it deliberately does not
docs.text:
:func:relocate_junction_vertices changes points and never triangles or labels. The connectivity is frozen, which is the whole argument for this construction over earlier attempts to improve junction geometry in this package: those moved tessellation points and let the Delaunay re-bracket the junction line, so the line could move the wrong way when the bracket changed. Here there is no bracket to change, and the treated mesh can be hashed against its own base.

The target is read from the mask, through :func:dw3d.junction_curves.extract_junction_curves, and only its matched curves are used -- the ones with exactly one counterpart among the mesh's own trijunctions of the same material triple. invented curves are never used as targets; fragmented curves are left untouched. No ground truth enters at any point: nothing here reads a reference mesh, a tension, a pressure or a Neumann angle, and the whole path has been re-run from a directory holding only the label image with a bit-identical result.

docs.title: Two guards, and why both are needed
docs.text:
Local. Moves are applied one vertex at a time in ascending vertex index, against the configuration as it stands rather than against the original, so two neighbouring junction vertices cannot both be accepted on the strength of a geometry neither will end up in. A move is accepted only if every triangle incident to that vertex keeps its normal orientation and keeps its area above :data:MIN_TRIANGLE_AREA, and if it leaves no cell on either side of those triangles with a signed volume of zero or less (a cell that already had one before the pass is not constrained). A rejected move is dropped, never repaired: the vertex stays where it was.

The cell clause exists because the triangle clause is blind to it: on a real embryo timepoint a cell made of a single tetrahedron had one vertex moved 6.7 voxels across the opposite face, every incident triangle kept a normal within 49 degrees of its previous one, and the cell's volume went from +35 to -5.8 cubic voxels. Its surface stayed closed, oriented, manifold and free of crossings, so no other check in the package saw it. The clause tests only the sign, deliberately: a floor at a fraction of the cell's volume before relocation was tried and refused more, because for the small cells that need it that volume is itself wrong, and a refused move freezes a vertex shared by several cells.

Nonlocal. A local guard cannot certify a nonlocal property. A move can drive one sheet of the mesh through a distant sheet while every triangle incident to the moved vertex stays perfectly oriented; measured on this package's benchmark cohort, all twelve local validity predicates stayed bit-identical on 40 of 40 cases while 23 such crossings existed on 5 of them. The second guard closes that: moving one vertex v changes the geometry of exactly the triangles incident to v, so every non-adjacent triangle pair with neither member incident to v has the same status before and after. The change in the whole-mesh crossing count therefore equals the change restricted to the pairs with at least one member incident to v -- an exact identity, not a neighbourhood approximation, because those partners range over the entire mesh. Accepting a move only when that restricted change is non-positive makes the crossing count non-increasing along the accepted sequence by construction.

That argument is checked rather than trusted: with verify=True the whole-mesh certificate of :mod:dw3d.triangle_intersection runs before and after, both counts are reported, and a rise raises rather than being absorbed.

docs.title: What this costs, and what it buys
docs.text: Measured over 40 equilibrium benchmark cases at four reconstruction spacings and on four point samplers, 16 independent adjudications. What the pass costs is best stated in seconds, because the reconstruction it follows varies by an order of magnitude between volumes: on the benchmark meshes, whose reconstruction takes about 5 s, it adds about 0.75 s (+15 %); on real embryo volumes, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s, it adds 0.1 to 1.5 s per timepoint (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on the two measured time series, +27 % to +208 %). Within one real series it grows faster than linearly with the number of triangles -- a fitted exponent of 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of mesh sizes in a fixed imaging volume, which describes that series and is not a tissue-scale law. About half of it is the nonlocal guard's candidate-pair search and a third the mask trijunction-curve extraction. The nonlocal guard refuses between 0.04 % and 0.21 % of the moves the local guard accepts, and that is enough to take the crossing count to zero everywhere. Line position error, local tangent error and discrete curvature all improve with their confidence intervals clear of zero at every spacing and on every sampler, and no pre-existing validity predicate changes on any case. On the seed-free samplers it also improves contact angles by 2.3 to 3.5 degrees and gauge-matched tension error by 20-40 %; on the seeded default sampler the line improves and the angle does not move significantly.

docs.title: Quadruple points
docs.text: A junction vertex lying on two or more matched trijunction lines has targets that disagree. The rule is to leave it where it is, and report how many there are. Nothing here invents a consensus position for such a vertex.

docs.title: Units and conventions
docs.text: All coordinates are mask voxel units -- the frame a reconstructed dw3d mesh's points live in and the frame :func:~dw3d.junction_curves.extract_junction_curves emits its polylines in. That extractor refuses a mesh whose coordinates do not lie inside the mask's extent, which catches most permuted axis orders; a mesh scaled down into the extent, or permuted on a mask whose sides are nearly equal, passes that check. Areas are square voxels. Vertex order, array shape and dtype are preserved exactly.

docs.title: Failure modes
docs.text: A mesh with no matched curve is returned unchanged with n_targets = 0; that is reported, not raised. A matched curve of fewer than two vertices carries no segment and is skipped and counted. A vertex with no incident triangle is skipped. The thresholds here are fixed and are not tuning parameters; they must not be adjusted to improve a reported metric.

docs.title: CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Junction relocation ran at a point spacing where its effect on tangent-based angles is unverified.

Emitted by :meth:dw3d.reconstruction_algorithm.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask once per reconstruction, when junction relocation is on (the default) and the point-placement function's min_distance is at least :data:COARSE_SPACING_MIN_DISTANCE. A placement function that carries no min_distance (a custom callable rather than one of the factory's functools.partial placements) never triggers it, because the spacing cannot be read.

What it means: at min_distance 5 the surface-tangent description of the contact angles moved by a small amount lying within the noise of the check that reads it, and no larger spacing has been measured. Facet-based contact angles improve at every spacing measured. The warning is a subclass of :class:UserWarning, so it can be silenced or promoted to an error on its own with :func:warnings.filterwarnings, and whether it fired is recorded in the algorithm's relocation_provenance. To reproduce the 0.4 behaviour, construct the algorithm with relocate_junctions=False or call set_junction_relocation(False) on the factory.

docs.title: build_vertex_pair_sets
docs.text:
build_vertex_pair_sets(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[integer], targets: dict[int, NDArray[float64]]) -> tuple[dict[int, NDArray[np.int64]], float]

For each vertex with a target, a superset of the pairs its move can change the status of.

The superset is built from the base centroids with an inflation that covers every displacement the pass can ever propose, so one static index serves the whole pass: a triangle's centroid moves by at most the largest displacement d of its own three vertices, its radius about that centroid grows by at most 2 d, and two triangles can meet only when their centroids lie within the sum of their radii. A pair that can ever meet therefore satisfies |c_f - c_t| <= r_f + r_t + 3 (d_f + d_t) at base. Writing reach = r + 3 d, the pairs of a vertex are every (f, t) with f incident to the vertex, t != f, |c_f - c_t| <= reach_f + reach_t (evaluated as np.linalg.norm of the centroid difference), and f and t sharing no vertex.

The neighbour search is one batched k-d tree search per pair of reach bins (:func:_neighbours_within_reach) rather than one ball query per triangle inflated by the mesh's largest reach; the exact criterion above then decides, so the pair sets are the same whatever the search proposes.

docs.title: Anisotropic masks
docs.text: Mask preprocessing before meshing: resampling a mask with anisotropic voxels to cubic voxels.

docs.title: Why this module exists
docs.text:
dw3d meshes a label image on its own voxel grid. When the voxels are longer along one axis (typically z) than along the other two, meshing on that grid and scaling the mesh afterwards samples the surfaces coarsely along the long axis: the junction triangles come out about k times taller (k = long spacing / short spacing) and their normals, hence every contact angle read from them, are off. Resampling the mask to cubic voxels by shape-based interpolation before meshing removes most of that error. Measured on masks down-sampled along z by k (each coarse voxel takes the label covering most of it), one meshing seed, as the median over cases of each mesh's median line-mean contact-angle error minus that of the same mask meshed at full resolution:

  • on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells voxelised at a real cell size (dw3d 0.7.0, before 0.8.0 pads thin margins of medium on the native grid; not measured again, because some of these runs need 8 to 40 GiB of memory): meshing the native grid costs +1.38 deg at k = 5/3, +1.97 at 2 and +4.10 at 3; resampling first, +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17;
  • on foambryo's benchmark, whose cells are larger (42 cases): native +1.59, +2.25 and +5.91 deg at k = 5/3, 2, 3 (dw3d 0.8.0, which pads the thin margins of 18 of the 42 masks at k = 3); resampled +0.43, +1.45 and +1.27 (dw3d 0.7.1; the resampled route is not padded by default).

Tension errors follow. Repeating slices (nearest neighbour) is worse than shape-based interpolation at every anisotropy above 2, and coarsening the two short axes, or passing the anisotropy to the distance transform alone, is worse than not resampling at all. Nothing was measured above k = 3 at real cell size. foambryo's quadric angle reading, which helps on the benchmark's larger cells, made every route worse at real cell size (dw3d 0.7.0's meshes): keep foambryo's default reading.

docs.title: Conventions
docs.text:
• spacing is the voxel size along the array's axes (axis 0, axis 1, axis 2), so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack, in any one unit. Exactly one axis may be coarser than the other two, which must be equal (to a relative SPACING_RELATIVE_TOLERANCE); this is the case of a microscope stack with its z step larger than its pixel size. Other spacings raise.
  • Frame: the centre of voxel j along an axis lies at j * spacing along that axis, so the first voxel of the input and of the output share their centre, and the output covers exactly the input's span between its first and last voxel centres. The output spacing is the short spacing h on every axis.
  • The output has the input's dtype and labels; no label is created.

docs.title: resample_to_isotropic
docs.text:
resample_to_isotropic(mask: NDArray, spacing: tuple[float, float, float], method: str = 'shape') -> NDArray

Resample a label mask with one coarse axis to cubic voxels of the short spacing.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask NDArray

3-D integer label image (0 = medium or background).

required spacing tuple[float, float, float]

voxel size along axes 0, 1, 2, so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack (see the module's conventions).

required method str

"shape" (default) or "nearest", see RESAMPLING_METHODS.

'shape'

Returns:

Type Description NDArray

The resampled mask, same dtype, on cubic voxels of size isotropic_spacing(spacing). Along the coarse axis

NDArray

it has floor((n - 1) k) + 1 voxels for n input voxels. **When the voxels are already cubic the input

NDArray

array itself is returned**, unchanged and uncopied, so an isotropic mask goes through bitwise.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for an unknown method, a mask that is not 3-D, or an unsupported spacing.

The shape-based method (Raya & Udupa, 1990): for every label, including 0, its 2-D signed distance is computed on every input slice across the coarse axis (positive inside, zero half-way between voxel centres) and interpolated linearly between slice centres; each output voxel takes the label with the largest value, ties to the smaller label. Where a label is present in one slice and absent from the next, the absent slice's value is min(d - k, -1/2) (d the present slice's): the surface keeps closing at one voxel per voxel, but never reaches the centre of a slice where the mask says the label is absent. Known bias: linear interpolation of a concave distance profile underestimates it, so small convex cells shrink slightly (measured on balls of radius 9-14 voxels: -1 to -5 % of their volume at k = 3, -5 to -11 % at k = 4). Each label is computed only in its bounding box (SHAPE_INTERPOLATION_MARGIN), so the cost grows with the cells' volume, not with the number of labels times the volume: about 40 s and 23 GiB for a 1 866-cell tissue of 4.98e8 voxels at k = 5/3. The measurements behind the choice are summarised in the module docstring.

docs.title: Masks from meshes
docs.text:
Rebuild a segmentation mask from a compressed segmentation (mesh, seeds and image shape).

Every voxel centre is assigned to the region of space the mesh's triangles enclose it in, and each region is named by the seed it holds (see dw3d.exact_voxelisation). The decision is exact and uses only the mesh's own triangles, so the rebuilt mask does not depend on the NumPy or SciPy version, nor on the machine. It approximates the original mask as closely as the mesh approximates the mask's interfaces; it is not a lossless copy.

Sacha Ichbiah, 2021. Matthieu Perez, 2024. Herve Turlier's group, 2026.

docs.title: reconstruct_mask_from_dict
docs.text:
reconstruct_mask_from_dict(dict_mask: dict[str]) -> NDArray[np.int64]

Reconstruct a segmentation image from a saved dict of points, triangles, seeds coords and desired image shape.

Each voxel centre takes the label of the region of space the mesh's triangles enclose it in: two neighbouring centres are in the same region when the segment between them crosses no triangle, and a region takes the index of the seed it holds. A centre lying exactly on a triangle belongs to the region it enters when moved infinitesimally towards increasing index along axis 0, then 1, then 2 (towards decreasing index on the last voxel of an axis, so that a cell cut by the image box keeps its outermost voxels). A region holding no seed (a few centres cut off by a sliver thinner than a voxel) takes the label of the region it shares the most neighbouring centres with. Every test is exact, so the result does not depend on the NumPy or SciPy version.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dict_mask dict[str]

the dictionary MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.last_compressed_segmentation returns, with keys points, triangles, seeds and image_shape. The points must be in voxel units of the mask, as the reconstruction returns them (not scaled by set_pixel_size or built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units). After construct_mesh_in_physical_units, divide the points by the resampled spacing (the shortest spacing) first: the seeds and image_shape are those of the resampled cubic grid, and that is the mask this rebuilds.

required

Returns:

Type Description NDArray[int64]

NDArray[np.int64]: the rebuilt mask, of shape image_shape, in 64-bit integer labels (not the original mask's dtype). Seed k (in the ascending label order of the original mask, label 0 included when present) fills its region with label k, so the labels are those of the original mask only when these were 0, 1, ..., n - 1.

docs.title: Decoupling the surface vertex set from the tesselation point set
docs.text:
dw3d's extraction is primal: a mesh triangle is a face of the tetrahedralisation, so every mesh vertex is a seed point. The boundary layer exploits that the other way round — it adds offset points a distance delta into each adjacent material precisely so that near-interface tetrahedra stop having all four vertices on the interface, which it achieves spectacularly (all-surface tets 40 % -> 0.8 %). But the offsets are then surface vertices too, and they sit delta voxels off the surface by design.

Measurement showed what that costs: the offsets are 30-35 % of mesh vertices, carry epsilon_rms = 2.51 voxels against the other families' 0.58-0.60, and account for 90 % of epsilon^2 — where epsilon is the vertex-to-true-surface distance that sets the junction-angle error through the calibrated error = C * epsilon / ell, C = 33.2 +- 1.2 deg.

exclude_offsets_from_surface removes them from the surface while leaving the tesselation, the watershed and the labelling untouched: each offset is merged onto its parent — the interface sample it is a delta-displacement of, which lies on the interface — and the triangles that collapse as a result are dropped. The surface vertex set becomes a subset of the interface samples and junction samples, i.e. of the points that were placed on the geometry, and the tesselation keeps every point it needs.

Two measurements decided this construction over the more literal alternative (move the vertex to "the EDT zero-set" along a tet edge):

  • The EDT has no zero-set at the interface. compute_edt_classical builds a valley, not a signed distance: interface samples sit at EDT 0.0-1.24 (median 0.82) with the level set by the local boundary thickness, and cell interiors are distance + max(edt_2). The interface is a local minimum set, so "project to the zero level set" is ill-posed; the well-posed operation is a 1-D minimisation across the sheet.
  • Doing that minimisation lands each offset 0.026 voxel (median) from an interface sample that is already a mesh vertex. The offsets carry no independent surface geometry: they are duplicates of the samples they were displaced from. Projecting them therefore produced 1234 triangles under 1 deg of minimum angle, 92 of exactly zero area and 409 normal flips on 3.tif alone — while merging them is exact, needs no interpolation and no threshold.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021. Matthieu Perez 2024.

labeled_mesh_from_labeled_graph(tesselation_graph: TesselationGraph, map_label_to_nodes_ids: dict[int, list[int]]) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.uint], NDArray[np.uint]]

Extract a labeled mesh from a labeled tesselation graph.

Winding convention. Every returned triangle has labels[i, 0] < labels[i, 1], and its right-hand-rule normal (p1 - p0) x (p2 - p0) points out of the region labels[i, 0] and into the region labels[i, 1]. This is the convention foambryo's cell volumes rely on (+det to the first label, -det to the second, by the divergence theorem). A triangle on the tesselation's hull (a border triangle, whose one tetrahedron carries a cell label) has labels (0, cell), so its normal points into the cell, i.e. into the hull.

docs.title: exclude_offsets_from_surface
docs.text:
exclude_offsets_from_surface(points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[uint], labels: NDArray[uint], surface_merge_target: NDArray[int64], guard_duplicate_faces: bool = True, collapse_rule: str = WELD) -> tuple[NDArray[np.uint], NDArray[np.uint], dict]

Merge every boundary-layer offset vertex onto its parent interface sample.

See the module docstring for why this is a merge and not a displacement. Each merge is a half-edge collapse, and they are independent: surface_merge_target is identity except on the offset families and no offset is ever another offset's target, so the merge itself is one vectorised re-indexing with no ordering to choose.

Geometry is not touched — no point moves — so points is returned to the caller unchanged and the surviving vertices keep the exact coordinates the tesselation gave them. What changes is which points the triangles reference.

Which merges are allowed is set by collapse_rule, and that is the whole difference between the unconditional weld and the link-condition-checked collapse:

  • "weld" (the historical, unconditional-merge behaviour) merges every offset it can, with only the duplicate-face guard below standing in the way. It is not topology preserving: welding two distinct vertices makes formerly distinct edges the same edge, so their triangle incidences add. Measured over the 51-case benchmark this took valence->=4 edges 115 -> 184 and abnormal non-manifold edges 7 -> 76.
  • "link_condition" (the topology-preserving rule) accepts a merge only when contracting the edge (offset, parent) cannot change the topology of the surface. See _refuse_by_link_condition for the three tests and why each is needed. It is the recommended rule; "weld" is kept reachable so the original offset-exclusion measurements stay reproducible.

The guard, and why it is on by default. ("weld" only — the link condition subsumes it, see condition 3 in _refuse_by_link_condition.) A few merges land two triangles on the same vertex triple: a flap flattened onto the film it hangs from. Measured three ways on 3.tif, keeping one copy of each such pair opens 4 boundary edges where the flap was what closed the surface; keeping both copies leaves 55 valence-4 edges (the coincident pairs) against the default's 0; dropping both opens 42. Refusing the handful of merges that would create a duplicate instead leaves the edge valence histogram identical to the default's (0 boundary edges, 227 valence-3, 0 valence-≥4) at the cost of leaving 38 of 650 offsets in the surface — 5.8 %, whose residual contribution to epsilon was measured separately. That is the trade taken, and guard_duplicate_faces=False reproduces the unguarded construction so it stays measurable rather than merely asserted.

The guard iterates because un-merging one offset can leave another duplicate behind; it converges in one round on every case measured, and GUARD_MAX_ROUNDS bounds it. Same-label duplicates that survive the guard are still deduplicated (one copy kept) so the return value is well defined either way.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default points NDArray[float64]

tesselation vertices (unchanged; read only to report the surface area before and after).

required triangles NDArray[uint]

extracted surface triangles, indexing points.

required labels NDArray[uint]

the (material, material) pair of each triangle.

required surface_merge_target NDArray[int64]

per tesselation point, the point the surface should use in its place; identity for every non-offset point. From the point-placing scheme's point_metadata (dw3d.points_on_edt).

required guard_duplicate_faces bool

refuse a merge that would put two triangles on one vertex triple. Defaults to True; see above. Ignored — and reported as ignored — when collapse_rule is "link_condition", which forbids the same thing on stronger grounds.

True collapse_rule str

"weld" (the unconditional-merge default, unchanged) or "link_condition" (the topology-preserving rule). See above.

WELD

Returns:

Type Description tuple[NDArray[uint], NDArray[uint], dict]

tuple[NDArray[np.uint], NDArray[np.uint], dict]: the re-indexed triangles, their labels, and a report: collapse_rule — the rule that was applied; n_triangles_before / n_triangles_after; n_triangles_collapsed — dropped for having a repeated vertex after the merge; n_merges_refused — offsets left in the surface by the guard or the link condition; n_guard_rounds — iterations the guard / link-condition sweep needed (0 when it is off or when there was nothing to refuse); n_refused_no_edge / n_refused_link_vertices / n_refused_link_edges / n_refused_valence — the link condition's refusal breakdown, all 0 under "weld"; see _refuse_by_link_condition; n_duplicate_triples — distinct vertex-triples still carrying more than one surviving triangle; n_duplicates_dropped — triangles dropped as same-label duplicates; n_duplicate_conflicts — duplicate triples whose triangles disagree on the label pair. Reported, not repaired: a conflict would mean the merge has fused two different interfaces, so it must be visible rather than silently deduplicated. n_surface_vertices_before / n_surface_vertices_after; n_offset_vertices_removed — surface vertices that were offsets and are gone; area_before / area_after.

docs.text:

Return a scaled points array from voxel coordinates to physical coordinates.

Given the microscope's xy and z pixel sizes. The points are in the mask's index order: column i is the voxel index along the mask's axis i. For a stack stored as (z, y, x), the usual order of a microscope stack and the one dw3d assumes, column 0 is scaled by z_pixel_size and columns 1 and 2 by xy_pixel_size.

Changed in 0.7.0: before, columns 0 and 1 were scaled by xy_pixel_size and column 2 by z_pixel_size, which multiplied z by the xy size and x by the z size. Results differ only when the two sizes differ.

For a mask whose voxels are longer along z, prefer MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units: it resamples the mask to cubic voxels before meshing, which is more accurate than meshing the native grid and scaling the mesh.
