docs.title: The dw3d package
docs.text:
Delaunay-Watershed 3D (dw3d): build a multimaterial surface mesh from a 3-D segmentation mask.

The top-level names build a reconstruction algorithm (get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm, MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory), save and reload its meshes, and read extra information from the mask (junction curves, crop faces, cell volumes).

Conventions used everywhere in the package:

  • The mask is a 3-D integer array; label 0 is the medium (the outside of the tissue), every other label is a cell.
  • Mesh points are in the mask's index order: column i of points is the position along the mask's axis i. For a microscope stack stored as (z, y, x), the order dw3d assumes, the points are (z, y, x). construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask returns them in voxel units: the centre of voxel (i, j, k) is the point (i, j, k).
  • spacing is the voxel size along the mask's axes 0, 1, 2, so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack.
  • labels[n] = (a, b), with a < b, are the two regions triangle n separates; its normal (right-hand rule on its three vertices) points out of a and into b: each triangle is the positively oriented boundary of a. dw2d's edges follow the same rule in their index order (row, column) (since 0.8.0; docs/user-guide/orientation-in-two-and-three-dimensions.md).
  • A 2-D mask given to the reconstruction is meshed by dw2d (MeshReconstructionAlgorithm's docstring).
  • min_distance (the point placement's minimum distance between points) counts voxels of the grid the mask is meshed on.

docs.title: UnresolvedCellWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Some regions of the mask are absent from the mesh.

Emitted once per reconstruction whose finished mesh lacks a label of the mask that was meshed, whatever the cause, naming each such region with its voxel count, the cause and the min_distance; the regions are the reconstruction's enclosed_medium_report.unresolved. A smaller min_distance may mesh them. The causes:

  • no tetrahedron centroid lies in the region's voxels (a cell a few voxels thick, or smaller than the point placement's min_distance). A region's watershed seed is the tetrahedron whose centroid is nearest to its deepest voxel; here that tetrahedron belongs to a neighbour, and before 0.7.1 the region grew from it inside the neighbour, as a phantom. Since 0.7.1 the seed is dropped.
  • the region was seeded, but the watershed left it few tetrahedra (often only its seed: the rest of the region, grouped without the seed, went to a neighbour) and mesh surgery relabelled those. Since 0.8.0 such a region is named too; before, only CellVolumeDisagreementWarning listed it, as a cell absent from the mesh.
  • the region had no watershed seed (label 0 when no piece of it touches the image box), or holds tetrahedra but no triangle of the finished mesh.

Every trijunction curve of one case, split by whether the mesh agrees it exists.

matched is the set a caller wanting usable geometry wants: on the benchmark at min_distance = 3 its 621 curves were measured a median 0.523 voxels from all three of their own interfaces at once, with a p99 of 4.43. docs.title: CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

Junction relocation ran at a point spacing where its effect on tangent-based angles is unverified.

Emitted by :meth:dw3d.reconstruction_algorithm.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask once per reconstruction, when junction relocation is on (the default) and the point-placement function's min_distance is at least :data:COARSE_SPACING_MIN_DISTANCE. A placement function that carries no min_distance (a custom callable rather than one of the factory's functools.partial placements) never triggers it, because the spacing cannot be read.

What it means: at min_distance 5 the surface-tangent description of the contact angles moved by a small amount lying within the noise of the check that reads it, and no larger spacing has been measured. Facet-based contact angles improve at every spacing measured. The warning is a subclass of :class:UserWarning, so it can be silenced or promoted to an error on its own with :func:warnings.filterwarnings, and whether it fired is recorded in the algorithm's relocation_provenance. To reproduce the 0.4 behaviour, construct the algorithm with relocate_junctions=False or call set_junction_relocation(False) on the factory.

docs.title: AbnormalEdgeWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A finished mesh still has abnormal non-manifold edges.

Emitted by :meth:dw3d.reconstruction_algorithm.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask once per reconstruction, when the final mesh has an edge carried by four or more triangles that do not separate as many regions (_find_abnormal_non_manifold_edges): a cell surface that touches itself, or two cells that meet twice, along that edge. The message gives their number and the configuration that made the mesh (point placement and its parameters, mesh surgery, tetrahedron order, offset exclusion). Such edges come from mesh surgery being off, from an edge surgery could not remove without adding another, or from a step after surgery (the offset exclusion of the boundary-layer configurations). Downstream, a junction reader may fail or skip that edge. A subclass of :class:UserWarning, so it can be silenced or promoted to an error on its own with :func:warnings.filterwarnings.

docs.title: MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory
docs.text:
MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory(print_info: bool = False, perform_mesh_postprocess_surgery: bool = True)

Factory to build custom algorithms for mesh reconstruction from segmentation masks.

Each set_* method chooses one step and returns the factory, so calls can be chained; make_algorithm builds the algorithm.

Initialize the factory with the steps of the deterministic configuration.

A new factory's make_algorithm builds what get_deterministic_algorithm returns: the classical EDT, deterministic EDT extrema with min_distance=3, plain Delaunay tesselation, max-value face scores, mesh surgery, junction relocation on, the canonical tetrahedron order and no physical image face. This is not get_default_algorithm, which places its points with the dithered rule (set_dithered_peak_local_points_placement_method).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default print_info bool

print the timing of each step. Defaults to False.

False perform_mesh_postprocess_surgery bool

try to detect and fix problems on the output mesh. Defaults to True.

True

docs.title: set_junction_relocation
docs.text:
set_junction_relocation(enabled: bool = True) -> Self

Choose whether the finished mesh's trijunction vertices move onto the mask's own trijunction curves.

On by default since 0.5.0, for this factory and for every get_*_algorithm static method. set_junction_relocation(False) switches it off and reproduces the 0.4 meshes exactly. The post-process is :func:dw3d.relocate_junction_vertices; it changes vertex positions only, never connectivity or labels, under a guard that provably cannot create a self-intersection anywhere in the mesh.

Cost, in seconds: about +0.75 s on the benchmark meshes (whose reconstruction takes about 5 s, +15 %); 0.1-1.5 s per timepoint on real embryo volumes (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two time series, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s). Within one real series it grows faster than linearly with mesh size (fitted exponent 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of triangle counts in a fixed volume -- a description of that series, not a tissue-scale law).

Measured over 40 equilibrium benchmark cases, four reconstruction spacings and four point samplers -- 16 independent adjudications, all passing: line position error, local tangent error and discrete curvature all improve with their intervals clear of zero, no pre-existing validity predicate changes, and the self-intersection count never rises. On the seed-free samplers it also improves contact angles by 2.3-3.5 degrees and gauge-matched tension error by 20-40 %; on the seeded default sampler the line improves and the angle does not move significantly. At a point-placement min_distance of 5 or more the reconstruction emits :class:dw3d.CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning once.

Parameters:

whether the post-process runs. Defaults to True, so that set_junction_relocation() reads as switching it on.

True

this factory, for chaining.

docs.title: get_default_algorithm staticmethod
docs.text:
get_default_algorithm(min_distance: int | None = None, print_info: bool = False) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the default mesh reconstruction algorithm with sensible default values.

This is get_dithered_algorithm at its own defaults: the published dw3d 0.3.6 configuration. The default was for a time the junction-protected, offset-excluded configuration (get_link_checked_algorithm); it went back to the dithered one because the end-to-end tension-inference accuracy that the meshing pipeline exists to serve is worse with the revised meshing than with the dithered configuration, on every method measured, despite the revised mesh's better geometric quality in isolation:

method dithered E_total (gauge-matched median) revised (link_checked) E_total YoungDupre 0.0763 0.1003 YoungDupreLocal 0.0911 0.1266 ForceBalanceKKT 0.1138 0.3262 BayesianMAP 0.1186 0.3149

(42 equilibrium cases of foambryo's benchmarking dataset, min_distance 3, dw3d 0.7.1, paired per case; see BENCHMARKS.md at the repository root.) The revised pipeline is real, deterministic, junction-protected and topologically cleaner than the dithered default by every meshing-only metric (interface-area bias, sliver fraction, score-gap degeneracy, non-manifold edges) -- it is kept, fully reachable, as an opt-in variant: get_link_checked_algorithm, a name that describes its mechanism (a link-condition-checked, topology-preserving offset collapse). Use it when meshing quality (junction placement, interface smoothness, topology) matters more than today's downstream tension-inference accuracy; use the default when tension inference is the goal, which is the common case.

Every configuration reachable from here keeps its own reference meshes and 51-case benchmark records:

  • get_link_checked_algorithm -- boundary layer + junction protection + link-checked offset exclusion; the opt-in "revised" variant, see above.
  • get_junction_protected_algorithm at its defaults -- boundary layer + junction protection alone, with the boundary-layer offsets left in the extracted surface. Carries a +15.7 % interface-area regression against ground truth that the link-checked exclusion removes; kept so it can be benchmarked against. (Its synonym get_offset_included_algorithm, deprecated since 0.5.0, was removed in 0.7.0.)
  • get_deterministic_algorithm -- deterministic EDT extrema only, plain Delaunay, no boundary layer or junction protection: the baseline the boundary-layer and junction-protection placements are measured against.

Every configuration, this one included, relocates junction vertices by default since 0.5.0; set relocate_junctions = False on the returned algorithm to reproduce 0.4. Every configuration puts the tetrahedra in canonical order by default since 0.7.1; set canonical_tetrahedron_order = False on the returned algorithm to keep Qhull's row order, as dw3d 0.7 did.

The EDT is compute_edt_classical. The tiled EDT (set_tiled_edt_method, reachable from a factory instance, not used here) produces a field whose values are bit-identical at a third of the peak RSS, and it is the variant to prefer at scale. Composition with a given reconstruction algorithm depends on whether that algorithm reads the EDT field's last bits (get_dithered_algorithm and get_deterministic_algorithm do not; get_link_checked_algorithm and its boundary-layer-derived relatives do, through the Hessian-eigenvector normals and the 27-sample face score interpolation -- see tests/test_edt_dtype_composition.py, and tests/test_edt_float64_tiling.py for the dtype=np.float64 variant that does compose with them at 8 bytes/voxel instead of 4).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_distance int | None

Minimum distance (in voxels of the grid the mask is meshed on) between extrema when placing tesselation points. Defaults to None: 3 voxels; a 2-D mask given to the algorithm is meshed by dw2d with 4 pixels, dw2d's default (an explicit value is used in both dimensions).

None print_info bool

Print algorithm details while executing. Defaults to False.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description MeshReconstructionAlgorithm MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

a new algorithm, with junction relocation on.

This is get_default_algorithm again (it was the default originally, then superseded for a time by the junction-protected and link-checked configurations, then restored): the revised meshing pipeline (get_link_checked_algorithm) produces better mesh geometry in isolation but worse end-to-end tension-inference accuracy on every method measured, so the dithered configuration ships as the default and the revised pipeline is the opt-in variant; see get_default_algorithm's docstring for the numbers.

The point placement is the historical randomly dithered one, so this reproduces the 0.3.6 point set exactly. The watershed's edge ordering is not reverted: the historical ordering was a sort with no tie-break over a score field that is ~30 % exactly tied, so it has no single well-defined answer to reproduce — it depended on numpy's sorting kernel. tests/golden/dithered/ records what this factory produces on the current stack, and is therefore a point-budget reference rather than a bit-for-bit replica of published output.

docs.title: get_junction_protected_algorithm staticmethod
docs.text:
get_junction_protected_algorithm(min_distance: int = 3, print_info: bool = False, delta: float | None = None, junction_spacing: float | None = None, shell_coarsening: int = 3, protect_radius: float | None = None, junction_delta: float | None = None, protect_junctions: bool = True, junction_boundary_layer: bool = False, use_weights: bool = True, spline_order: int = 1, exclude_offsets_from_surface: bool = False, guard_duplicate_faces: bool = True, collapse_rule: str = WELD) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the junction-protected reconstruction algorithm.

This is the configuration get_default_algorithm returned for a time before the link-checked offset exclusion became the default (its former synonym get_offset_included_algorithm was removed in 0.7.0). It is the only way to reach the ablation switches below, and the corresponding benchmark records are keyed on it. This configuration plus the link-checked offset exclusion (get_link_checked_algorithm) is reachable from here as exclude_offsets_from_surface=True, collapse_rule=LINK_CONDITION.

The boundary layer plus 0-/1-junction detection, protecting balls and shell coarsening, tesselated by the regular (weighted) triangulation that consumes the protecting-ball radii. The boundary layer and junction protection are assessed as a pair, so this getter is that combined configuration; get_boundary_layer_algorithm remains the boundary layer alone and get_deterministic_algorithm is the configuration that predates both.

Two defaults differ from the junction-protection scheme as first designed, both on measured grounds:

  • junction_boundary_layer=False. The first design asks for the boundary layer around junction samples too, on the grounds that it prevents the "more points locally -> more small tets" failure. Measured over 11 cases it causes that failure: it takes valence->=4 edges 33 -> 119 and abnormal non-manifold edges 2 -> 91, essentially all of the added valence->=4 edges being the 3-material (pinched-triple-line) kind. The mechanism is structural, not a bad constant: the junction offsets refill the protecting balls that the same construction has just emptied, and a protecting ball only protects while it stays empty. The layer is implemented and reachable with junction_boundary_layer=True so the originally specified configuration stays reproducible.
  • shell_coarsening=3. Off (1) is a valid configuration and meets the topology criteria too; 3 is chosen for the point budget and wall time, not to make any acceptance criterion pass, on the strength of a sweep over the coarsening factor.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_distance int

Minimum distance between extrema. Defaults to 3.

3 print_info bool

Print algorithm details while executing.

False delta float | None

Boundary-layer offset distance. Defaults to min_distance when None.

None junction_spacing float | None

h_J; defaults to 2*min_distance + 1 when None.

None shell_coarsening int

Shell re-packing factor; 1 is off. Defaults to 3.

3 protect_radius float | None

Protecting-ball radius. Defaults to junction_spacing / 2.

None junction_delta float | None

Junction boundary-layer offset distance. Defaults to protect_radius.

None protect_junctions bool

Ablation switch; see dw3d.points_on_edt.junction_protected_families. Defaults to True.

True junction_boundary_layer bool

Ablation switch; True restores the junction-protection scheme as first designed. Defaults to False — see above.

False use_weights bool

Ablation switch — False tesselates the same point set with plain Delaunay, isolating the regular triangulation's own contribution. Defaults to True.

True spline_order int

EDT interpolation order for the watershed scores; 3 selects the cubic B-spline. Defaults to 1, trilinear, which is what the default algorithm uses. See dw3d.score_computation.

1 exclude_offsets_from_surface bool

Keep the boundary-layer offsets in the tesselation and out of the extracted surface. The tesselation, the watershed and the labelling are bit-identical either way. Defaults to False.

False guard_duplicate_faces bool

Offset-exclusion ablation switch — refuse the merges that would duplicate a face. False reproduces the unguarded construction, which trades 4 boundary edges for 38 fewer offsets on 3.tif. Defaults to True. Ignored under the "link_condition" collapse rule, which forbids the same thing.

True collapse_rule str

"weld" merges every offset it can (the unconditional-merge rule, which regressed valence->=4 edges 115 -> 184 and abnormal non-manifold edges 7 -> 76), "link_condition" accepts only the merges that cannot change the surface topology. See dw3d.mesh_utilities.exclude_offsets_from_surface. Defaults to "weld" so that the unconditional-merge benchmark records stay reproducible; get_link_checked_algorithm is the link-condition configuration.

WELD

Returns:

Name Type Description MeshReconstructionAlgorithm MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

a new algorithm, with junction relocation on.

docs.title: get_link_checked_algorithm staticmethod
docs.text:
get_link_checked_algorithm(min_distance: int = 3, print_info: bool = False, spline_order: int = 1) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the "revised meshing" variant: junction-protected with a topology-preserving offset collapse.

This was get_default_algorithm for a time, until the default went back to the dithered configuration because end-to-end tension-inference accuracy is worse with this pipeline than with the dithered one on every method measured, despite its better mesh quality in isolation (interface-area bias, sliver fraction, junction placement, topology -- see get_default_algorithm's docstring for the numbers). It is deterministic, junction-protected and topologically corrected relative to the dithered configuration; "link-checked" names its mechanism (a link-condition-checked, topology-preserving offset collapse). Use it when mesh geometry and topology matter more than today's downstream tension-inference accuracy. Its benchmark records are keyed on the variant name offset_excluded_linkcheck.

Identical to get_junction_protected_algorithm(exclude_offsets_from_surface=True) except that each offset is removed from the surface by a link-condition-checked edge contraction rather than an unconditional weld. Same EDT, same point set, same regular triangulation, same watershed, same mesh surgery, same set of candidate merges — only the test that decides which candidates are taken differs.

Why this exists. The unconditional weld bought a large geometric improvement (the offset-included default over-estimates every interface area by +15.7 %, the weld-based exclusion by +1.2 %) at the cost of a real topological regression: welding two vertices makes formerly distinct edges the same edge, so their triangle incidences add, and over the 51-case benchmark that took valence->=4 edges 115 -> 184 and abnormal non-manifold edges 7 -> 76. The link-condition-checked collapse refuses exactly the merges that would do that; see dw3d.mesh_utilities._refuse_by_link_condition for the four tests, and for the non-manifold counterexample showing why the classical link condition alone is not sufficient here.

It refuses fewer merges than the duplicate-face guard on the unconditional weld, not more, because retrying a refused candidate once its neighbours have collapsed recovers most of them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_distance int

Minimum distance between extrema. Defaults to 3.

3 print_info bool

Print algorithm details while executing.

False spline_order int

EDT interpolation order for the watershed scores; 3 composes this collapse rule with the cubic B-spline. Defaults to 1.

1

Returns:

Name Type Description MeshReconstructionAlgorithm MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

a new algorithm, with junction relocation on.

docs.title: extract_junction_curves
docs.text:
extract_junction_curves(segmented_mask: NDArray[uint], points: NDArray[float64], triangles: NDArray[int64], labels: NDArray[int64], *, estimator: Estimator = 'plain') -> JunctionCurves

Trijunction curves from the mask, keyed to the mesh's own trijunctions.

The one line a user writes::

curves = extract_junction_curves(mask, *load_rec("000_mesh.rec"))

curves.matched is the usable set. Every one of its members has exactly one counterpart among the mesh's own trijunctions of the same material triple, so it can be joined to the interfaces and the dihedral angles the reconstruction already reports. curves.invented is everything the mask says is a junction and the mesh does not have; none of 27 of those were measured within one voxel of all three of their interfaces, against a median of 0.524 voxels for the matched ones, so they are kept apart rather than merged. curves.fragmented holds real trijunctions the mask resolves as several pieces.

Reading spacing is not a parameter: the polylines are resampled at the mesh's own median trijunction-edge length, so accuracy is compared at the resolution the mesh states its lines at rather than at whatever resolution the lattice happens to give.

Cost, and why "plain" is the default. "plain" is detection only -- no linear program -- and costs about 0.8 s per benchmark case against the 1.49 s dw3d spends reconstructing that case. "anchor" solves one small linear program per returned vertex and costs roughly fifteen times as much, about eight times the whole reconstruction it annotates, and buys 9-11 % of the position error. Nobody meshing a large tissue should pay that by default, so they do not.

"anchor"'s real argument is not that 9 %: it is that the polytope's deepest interior point carries only the irreducible narrow-wedge term (a) of the mask's identifiability floor, where the detected position and the centroid both carry more. Reach for it when a systematic bias against narrow wedges would corrupt what you are inferring, not to shave a tenth of a voxel. "centroid" is kept for comparison only: it was measured carrying (a) + (b), so it is the larger systematic, not the smaller one, and it costs about thirty times the anchor's linear programs on top.

the label image the mesh was reconstructed from.

triangle vertex indices, (m, 3).

required labels NDArray[int64]

the two materials each triangle separates, (m, 2).

required estimator Estimator

"plain" (default, no linear program), "anchor" or "centroid". See the cost paragraph above before changing it.

'plain'

Type Description ValueError

if estimator is not one of the three, or if the mesh's coordinates do not lie inside the mask's extent.

Returns:

docs.title: resample_to_isotropic
docs.text:
resample_to_isotropic(mask: NDArray, spacing: tuple[float, float, float], method: str = 'shape') -> NDArray

Resample a label mask with one coarse axis to cubic voxels of the short spacing.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default mask NDArray

3-D integer label image (0 = medium or background).

required spacing tuple[float, float, float]

voxel size along axes 0, 1, 2, so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack (see the module's conventions).

required method str

"shape" (default) or "nearest", see RESAMPLING_METHODS.

'shape'

Returns:

Type Description NDArray

The resampled mask, same dtype, on cubic voxels of size isotropic_spacing(spacing). Along the coarse axis

NDArray

it has floor((n - 1) k) + 1 voxels for n input voxels. **When the voxels are already cubic the input

NDArray

array itself is returned**, unchanged and uncopied, so an isotropic mask goes through bitwise.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for an unknown method, a mask that is not 3-D, or an unsupported spacing.

The shape-based method (Raya & Udupa, 1990): for every label, including 0, its 2-D signed distance is computed on every input slice across the coarse axis (positive inside, zero half-way between voxel centres) and interpolated linearly between slice centres; each output voxel takes the label with the largest value, ties to the smaller label. Where a label is present in one slice and absent from the next, the absent slice's value is min(d - k, -1/2) (d the present slice's): the surface keeps closing at one voxel per voxel, but never reaches the centre of a slice where the mask says the label is absent. Known bias: linear interpolation of a concave distance profile underestimates it, so small convex cells shrink slightly (measured on balls of radius 9-14 voxels: -1 to -5 % of their volume at k = 3, -5 to -11 % at k = 4). Each label is computed only in its bounding box (SHAPE_INTERPOLATION_MARGIN), so the cost grows with the cells' volume, not with the number of labels times the volume: about 40 s and 23 GiB for a 1 866-cell tissue of 4.98e8 voxels at k = 5/3. The measurements behind the choice are summarised in the module docstring.

docs.title: reconstruct_mask_from_dict
docs.text:
reconstruct_mask_from_dict(dict_mask: dict[str]) -> NDArray[np.int64]

Reconstruct a segmentation image from a saved dict of points, triangles, seeds coords and desired image shape.

Each voxel centre takes the label of the region of space the mesh's triangles enclose it in: two neighbouring centres are in the same region when the segment between them crosses no triangle, and a region takes the index of the seed it holds. A centre lying exactly on a triangle belongs to the region it enters when moved infinitesimally towards increasing index along axis 0, then 1, then 2 (towards decreasing index on the last voxel of an axis, so that a cell cut by the image box keeps its outermost voxels). A region holding no seed (a few centres cut off by a sliver thinner than a voxel) takes the label of the region it shares the most neighbouring centres with. Every test is exact, so the result does not depend on the NumPy or SciPy version.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default dict_mask dict[str]

the dictionary MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.last_compressed_segmentation returns, with keys points, triangles, seeds and image_shape. The points must be in voxel units of the mask, as the reconstruction returns them (not scaled by set_pixel_size or built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units). After construct_mesh_in_physical_units, divide the points by the resampled spacing (the shortest spacing) first: the seeds and image_shape are those of the resampled cubic grid, and that is the mask this rebuilds.

required

Returns:

Type Description NDArray[int64]

NDArray[np.int64]: the rebuilt mask, of shape image_shape, in 64-bit integer labels (not the original mask's dtype). Seed k (in the ascending label order of the original mask, label 0 included when present) fills its region with label k, so the labels are those of the original mask only when these were 0, 1, ..., n - 1.

docs.title: Reconstruction algorithms
docs.text:
Build mesh reconstruction algorithms: the named configurations and a factory for custom ones.

MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory's static get_*_algorithm methods return the named configurations (get_default_algorithm is the one to use for tension inference); an instance of the factory combines the steps one by one and make_algorithm builds the result.

Matthieu Perez 2024

The mesh reconstruction algorithm: from a 3-D segmentation mask to a multimaterial surface mesh.

MeshReconstructionAlgorithm runs the pipeline (distance transform, point placement, tesselation, seeded watershed, mesh extraction and surgery, crop-face marking, junction relocation, cell-volume check) and keeps the last mesh it built. Get one from dw3d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory or dw3d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm.

Sacha Ichbiah 2021 Matthieu Perez 2024

docs.text:
MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory(print_info: bool = False, perform_mesh_postprocess_surgery: bool = True)

Factory to build custom algorithms for mesh reconstruction from segmentation masks.

Each set_* method chooses one step and returns the factory, so calls can be chained; make_algorithm builds the algorithm.

Initialize the factory with the steps of the deterministic configuration.

A new factory's make_algorithm builds what get_deterministic_algorithm returns: the classical EDT, deterministic EDT extrema with min_distance=3, plain Delaunay tesselation, max-value face scores, mesh surgery, junction relocation on, the canonical tetrahedron order and no physical image face. This is not get_default_algorithm, which places its points with the dithered rule (set_dithered_peak_local_points_placement_method).

docs.title: set_junction_relocation
docs.text:
set_junction_relocation(enabled: bool = True) -> Self

Choose whether the finished mesh's trijunction vertices move onto the mask's own trijunction curves.

On by default since 0.5.0, for this factory and for every get_*_algorithm static method. set_junction_relocation(False) switches it off and reproduces the 0.4 meshes exactly. The post-process is :func:dw3d.relocate_junction_vertices; it changes vertex positions only, never connectivity or labels, under a guard that provably cannot create a self-intersection anywhere in the mesh.

Cost, in seconds: about +0.75 s on the benchmark meshes (whose reconstruction takes about 5 s, +15 %); 0.1-1.5 s per timepoint on real embryo volumes (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two time series, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s). Within one real series it grows faster than linearly with mesh size (fitted exponent 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range of triangle counts in a fixed volume -- a description of that series, not a tissue-scale law).

Measured over 40 equilibrium benchmark cases, four reconstruction spacings and four point samplers -- 16 independent adjudications, all passing: line position error, local tangent error and discrete curvature all improve with their intervals clear of zero, no pre-existing validity predicate changes, and the self-intersection count never rises. On the seed-free samplers it also improves contact angles by 2.3-3.5 degrees and gauge-matched tension error by 20-40 %; on the seeded default sampler the line improves and the angle does not move significantly. At a point-placement min_distance of 5 or more the reconstruction emits :class:dw3d.CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning once.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default enabled bool

whether the post-process runs. Defaults to True, so that set_junction_relocation() reads as switching it on.

True

Returns:

Name Type Description Self Self

this factory, for chaining.

Choose whether the tesselation's tetrahedra are put in canonical order before anything reads them.

On by default since 0.7.1, for this factory and for every get_*_algorithm static method. The canonical order sorts the vertex indices within each tetrahedron and the tetrahedra lexicographically (dw3d.tesselation.canonical_tetrahedron_order), so the mesh no longer depends on the row order in which Qhull returns the same tetrahedra. set_canonical_tetrahedron_order(False) keeps Qhull's row order, which reproduces the meshes of dw3d 0.7 and earlier on the machine they were made on. See MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.__init__ for what the row order changes.

docs.title: get_default_algorithm staticmethod
docs.text:
get_default_algorithm(min_distance: int | None = None, print_info: bool = False) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the default mesh reconstruction algorithm with sensible default values.

This is get_dithered_algorithm at its own defaults: the published dw3d 0.3.6 configuration. The default was for a time the junction-protected, offset-excluded configuration (get_link_checked_algorithm); it went back to the dithered one because the end-to-end tension-inference accuracy that the meshing pipeline exists to serve is worse with the revised meshing than with the dithered configuration, on every method measured, despite the revised mesh's better geometric quality in isolation:

method dithered E_total (gauge-matched median) revised (link_checked) E_total YoungDupre 0.0763 0.1003 YoungDupreLocal 0.0911 0.1266 ForceBalanceKKT 0.1138 0.3262 BayesianMAP 0.1186 0.3149

(42 equilibrium cases of foambryo's benchmarking dataset, min_distance 3, dw3d 0.7.1, paired per case; see BENCHMARKS.md at the repository root.) The revised pipeline is real, deterministic, junction-protected and topologically cleaner than the dithered default by every meshing-only metric (interface-area bias, sliver fraction, score-gap degeneracy, non-manifold edges) -- it is kept, fully reachable, as an opt-in variant: get_link_checked_algorithm, a name that describes its mechanism (a link-condition-checked, topology-preserving offset collapse). Use it when meshing quality (junction placement, interface smoothness, topology) matters more than today's downstream tension-inference accuracy; use the default when tension inference is the goal, which is the common case.

Every configuration reachable from here keeps its own reference meshes and 51-case benchmark records:

  • get_link_checked_algorithm -- boundary layer + junction protection + link-checked offset exclusion; the opt-in "revised" variant, see above.
  • get_junction_protected_algorithm at its defaults -- boundary layer + junction protection alone, with the boundary-layer offsets left in the extracted surface. Carries a +15.7 % interface-area regression against ground truth that the link-checked exclusion removes; kept so it can be benchmarked against. (Its synonym get_offset_included_algorithm, deprecated since 0.5.0, was removed in 0.7.0.)
  • get_deterministic_algorithm -- deterministic EDT extrema only, plain Delaunay, no boundary layer or junction protection: the baseline the boundary-layer and junction-protection placements are measured against.

Every configuration, this one included, relocates junction vertices by default since 0.5.0; set relocate_junctions = False on the returned algorithm to reproduce 0.4. Every configuration puts the tetrahedra in canonical order by default since 0.7.1; set canonical_tetrahedron_order = False on the returned algorithm to keep Qhull's row order, as dw3d 0.7 did.

The EDT is compute_edt_classical. The tiled EDT (set_tiled_edt_method, reachable from a factory instance, not used here) produces a field whose values are bit-identical at a third of the peak RSS, and it is the variant to prefer at scale. Composition with a given reconstruction algorithm depends on whether that algorithm reads the EDT field's last bits (get_dithered_algorithm and get_deterministic_algorithm do not; get_link_checked_algorithm and its boundary-layer-derived relatives do, through the Hessian-eigenvector normals and the 27-sample face score interpolation -- see tests/test_edt_dtype_composition.py, and tests/test_edt_float64_tiling.py for the dtype=np.float64 variant that does compose with them at 8 bytes/voxel instead of 4).

Parameters:

Minimum distance (in voxels of the grid the mask is meshed on) between extrema when placing tesselation points. Defaults to None: 3 voxels; a 2-D mask given to the algorithm is meshed by dw2d with 4 pixels, dw2d's default (an explicit value is used in both dimensions).

None print_info bool

Print algorithm details while executing. Defaults to False.

False

Returns:

Name Type Description MeshReconstructionAlgorithm MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

a new algorithm, with junction relocation on.

get_dithered_algorithm(min_distance: int | None = None, print_info: bool = False, seed: int = 42) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the reconstruction algorithm as it was in dw3d 0.3.6, before point placement was made deterministic.

This is get_default_algorithm again (it was the default originally, then superseded for a time by the junction-protected and link-checked configurations, then restored): the revised meshing pipeline (get_link_checked_algorithm) produces better mesh geometry in isolation but worse end-to-end tension-inference accuracy on every method measured, so the dithered configuration ships as the default and the revised pipeline is the opt-in variant; see get_default_algorithm's docstring for the numbers.

The point placement is the historical randomly dithered one, so this reproduces the 0.3.6 point set exactly. The watershed's edge ordering is not reverted: the historical ordering was a sort with no tie-break over a score field that is ~30 % exactly tied, so it has no single well-defined answer to reproduce — it depended on numpy's sorting kernel. tests/golden/dithered/ records what this factory produces on the current stack, and is therefore a point-budget reference rather than a bit-for-bit replica of published output.

docs.title: get_junction_protected_algorithm staticmethod
docs.text:
get_junction_protected_algorithm(min_distance: int = 3, print_info: bool = False, delta: float | None = None, junction_spacing: float | None = None, shell_coarsening: int = 3, protect_radius: float | None = None, junction_delta: float | None = None, protect_junctions: bool = True, junction_boundary_layer: bool = False, use_weights: bool = True, spline_order: int = 1, exclude_offsets_from_surface: bool = False, guard_duplicate_faces: bool = True, collapse_rule: str = WELD) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the junction-protected reconstruction algorithm.

This is the configuration get_default_algorithm returned for a time before the link-checked offset exclusion became the default (its former synonym get_offset_included_algorithm was removed in 0.7.0). It is the only way to reach the ablation switches below, and the corresponding benchmark records are keyed on it. This configuration plus the link-checked offset exclusion (get_link_checked_algorithm) is reachable from here as exclude_offsets_from_surface=True, collapse_rule=LINK_CONDITION.

The boundary layer plus 0-/1-junction detection, protecting balls and shell coarsening, tesselated by the regular (weighted) triangulation that consumes the protecting-ball radii. The boundary layer and junction protection are assessed as a pair, so this getter is that combined configuration; get_boundary_layer_algorithm remains the boundary layer alone and get_deterministic_algorithm is the configuration that predates both.

Two defaults differ from the junction-protection scheme as first designed, both on measured grounds:

  • junction_boundary_layer=False. The first design asks for the boundary layer around junction samples too, on the grounds that it prevents the "more points locally -> more small tets" failure. Measured over 11 cases it causes that failure: it takes valence->=4 edges 33 -> 119 and abnormal non-manifold edges 2 -> 91, essentially all of the added valence->=4 edges being the 3-material (pinched-triple-line) kind. The mechanism is structural, not a bad constant: the junction offsets refill the protecting balls that the same construction has just emptied, and a protecting ball only protects while it stays empty. The layer is implemented and reachable with junction_boundary_layer=True so the originally specified configuration stays reproducible.
  • shell_coarsening=3. Off (1) is a valid configuration and meets the topology criteria too; 3 is chosen for the point budget and wall time, not to make any acceptance criterion pass, on the strength of a sweep over the coarsening factor.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_distance int

Minimum distance between extrema. Defaults to 3.

3 print_info bool

Print algorithm details while executing.

False delta float | None

Boundary-layer offset distance. Defaults to min_distance when None.

None junction_spacing float | None

h_J; defaults to 2*min_distance + 1 when None.

None shell_coarsening int

Shell re-packing factor; 1 is off. Defaults to 3.

3 protect_radius float | None

Protecting-ball radius. Defaults to junction_spacing / 2.

None junction_delta float | None

Junction boundary-layer offset distance. Defaults to protect_radius.

None protect_junctions bool

Ablation switch; see dw3d.points_on_edt.junction_protected_families. Defaults to True.

True junction_boundary_layer bool

Ablation switch; True restores the junction-protection scheme as first designed. Defaults to False — see above.

False use_weights bool

Ablation switch — False tesselates the same point set with plain Delaunay, isolating the regular triangulation's own contribution. Defaults to True.

True spline_order int

EDT interpolation order for the watershed scores; 3 selects the cubic B-spline. Defaults to 1, trilinear, which is what the default algorithm uses. See dw3d.score_computation.

1 exclude_offsets_from_surface bool

Keep the boundary-layer offsets in the tesselation and out of the extracted surface. The tesselation, the watershed and the labelling are bit-identical either way. Defaults to False.

False guard_duplicate_faces bool

Offset-exclusion ablation switch — refuse the merges that would duplicate a face. False reproduces the unguarded construction, which trades 4 boundary edges for 38 fewer offsets on 3.tif. Defaults to True. Ignored under the "link_condition" collapse rule, which forbids the same thing.

True collapse_rule str

"weld" merges every offset it can (the unconditional-merge rule, which regressed valence->=4 edges 115 -> 184 and abnormal non-manifold edges 7 -> 76), "link_condition" accepts only the merges that cannot change the surface topology. See dw3d.mesh_utilities.exclude_offsets_from_surface. Defaults to "weld" so that the unconditional-merge benchmark records stay reproducible; get_link_checked_algorithm is the link-condition configuration.

WELD

Returns:

Name Type Description MeshReconstructionAlgorithm MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

a new algorithm, with junction relocation on.

docs.title: get_link_checked_algorithm staticmethod
docs.text:
get_link_checked_algorithm(min_distance: int = 3, print_info: bool = False, spline_order: int = 1) -> MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

Return the "revised meshing" variant: junction-protected with a topology-preserving offset collapse.

This was get_default_algorithm for a time, until the default went back to the dithered configuration because end-to-end tension-inference accuracy is worse with this pipeline than with the dithered one on every method measured, despite its better mesh quality in isolation (interface-area bias, sliver fraction, junction placement, topology -- see get_default_algorithm's docstring for the numbers). It is deterministic, junction-protected and topologically corrected relative to the dithered configuration; "link-checked" names its mechanism (a link-condition-checked, topology-preserving offset collapse). Use it when mesh geometry and topology matter more than today's downstream tension-inference accuracy. Its benchmark records are keyed on the variant name offset_excluded_linkcheck.

Identical to get_junction_protected_algorithm(exclude_offsets_from_surface=True) except that each offset is removed from the surface by a link-condition-checked edge contraction rather than an unconditional weld. Same EDT, same point set, same regular triangulation, same watershed, same mesh surgery, same set of candidate merges — only the test that decides which candidates are taken differs.

Why this exists. The unconditional weld bought a large geometric improvement (the offset-included default over-estimates every interface area by +15.7 %, the weld-based exclusion by +1.2 %) at the cost of a real topological regression: welding two vertices makes formerly distinct edges the same edge, so their triangle incidences add, and over the 51-case benchmark that took valence->=4 edges 115 -> 184 and abnormal non-manifold edges 7 -> 76. The link-condition-checked collapse refuses exactly the merges that would do that; see dw3d.mesh_utilities._refuse_by_link_condition for the four tests, and for the non-manifold counterexample showing why the classical link condition alone is not sufficient here.

It refuses fewer merges than the duplicate-face guard on the unconditional weld, not more, because retrying a refused candidate once its neighbours have collapsed recovers most of them.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default min_distance int

Minimum distance between extrema. Defaults to 3.

3 print_info bool

Print algorithm details while executing.

False spline_order int

EDT interpolation order for the watershed scores; 3 composes this collapse rule with the cubic B-spline. Defaults to 1.

1

Returns:

Name Type Description MeshReconstructionAlgorithm MeshReconstructionAlgorithm

a new algorithm, with junction relocation on.

docs.title: MeshReconstructionAlgorithm
docs.text:
MeshReconstructionAlgorithm(print_info: bool, edt_creation_function: EdtCreationFunction, point_placing_function: PointPlacingFunction, tesselation_creation_function: TesselationCreationFunction, score_computation_function: ScoreComputationFunction, perform_mesh_postprocess_surgery: bool, relocate_junctions: bool = True, physical_image_faces: tuple[str, ...] = (), canonical_tetrahedron_order: bool = True, label_enclosed_media: bool = True, pad_thin_medium_margins: bool = True)

Algorithm that builds a multimaterial surface mesh from a 3-D segmentation mask (and a 2-D mesh from a 2-D one).

A 2-D mask given to construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask or construct_mesh_in_physical_units is meshed by dw2d (imported then, on first use): the algorithm builds a dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm from its settings that have a 2-D meaning (min_distance, junction relocation, canonical order, print_info) and returns dw2d's (points (n, 2), segments (m, 2), labels (m, 2)). Until the object meets a 3-D mask again, last_constructed_mesh, last_compressed_segmentation, save_to_rec_mesh, relocation_report, cut_cells and medium_labels are dw2d's, two_dimensional_algorithm is that object, and the 3-D-only reports (crop_faces, crop_face_report, cell_volume_report, enclosed_medium_report) are None. min_distance is the one given to the factory, or dw2d's default (4 pixels) when none was given (requested_min_distance). A configuration with no 2-D meaning (boundary-layer, junction-protected or link-checked placement, another EDT, tesselation or face score, physical image faces, mesh surgery off) raises ValueError naming it; the default (dithered) and the deterministic placements are both meshed by dw2d's placement, which has no dither. See _mask_dimension for the input checks.

Build one with dw3d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory (or one of its get_*_algorithm methods) rather than by calling the constructor. The same object can reconstruct several masks; each reconstruction replaces the last mesh and every report about it.

The mesh is (points, triangles, labels): points (n, 3) float64, in the mask's index order ((z, y, x) for a (z, y, x) stack) and in voxel units unless built by construct_mesh_in_physical_units; triangles (m, 3) vertex indices; labels (m, 2), the two regions each triangle separates, smaller label first, label 0 being the medium.

Attributes:

Name Type Description print_info bool

whether to print the timing of each step.

relocate_junctions bool

whether the next reconstruction runs junction relocation.

canonical_tetrahedron_order bool

whether the next reconstruction puts the tetrahedra in canonical order before anything reads them; see __init__.

physical_image_faces tuple[str, ...]

the image faces declared physical; see __init__.

Set the methods used by this algorithm to reconstruct a mesh from a segmentation mask.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default print_info bool

Whether to show details about the computation during the algorithm's execution.

required edt_creation_function EdtCreationFunction

Function used to compute an EDT from the segmentation mask.

required point_placing_function PointPlacingFunction

Function used to place points on the EDT for a tesselation.

required tesselation_creation_function TesselationCreationFunction

Function used to tesselate the points.

required score_computation_function ScoreComputationFunction

Function used to compute the scores for Watershed.

required perform_mesh_postprocess_surgery bool

Whether to try to detect and fix problems on the output mesh.

required relocate_junctions bool

Whether to move the finished mesh's trijunction vertices onto the trijunction curves the mask itself gives, as a post-process. Defaults to True since 0.5.0. False reproduces the 0.4 meshes exactly. The post-process is dw3d.relocate_junction_vertices; it changes vertex positions only, never connectivity or labels, under a guard that cannot create a self-intersection. Cost, in seconds: about +0.75 s on the benchmark meshes (whose reconstruction takes about 5 s, +15 %), and 0.1-1.5 s per timepoint on real embryo volumes (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two time series, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s); within one real series it grows faster than linearly with mesh size. See dw3d.junction_relocation for what it was measured to buy, relocation_report for what it did on the last mesh, and relocation_provenance for whether it ran and whether CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning fired. At a point-placement min_distance of 5 or more it emits that warning once per reconstruction.

True physical_image_faces tuple[str, ...]

the faces of the image box, among dw3d.crop_faces.IMAGE_FACES ("axis0_low", "axis0_high", ... "axis2_high"), where the tissue really ends, for example on a coverslip. A cell surface lying on such a face is contact with the medium. Defaults to none: every image face is a crop, the triangles a cell has on it are crop faces (crop_faces) where the mask's cell reaches that face, and the cells they touch are cut cells (cut_cells). Can also be set as an attribute before a reconstruction. Changes no point, triangle or label of the mesh; see dw3d.crop_faces.

() canonical_tetrahedron_order bool

Whether to put the tesselation's tetrahedra in canonical order (dw3d.tesselation.canonical_tetrahedron_order: vertex indices sorted within each tetrahedron, tetrahedra sorted lexicographically) before anything reads them. Defaults to True since 0.7.1. The tetrahedra's row indices break the watershed's ties between exactly equal face scores (about a third of the score field is exactly tied), pick the seed tetrahedra and order mesh surgery's cycles, and the row order Qhull returns is not a function of the tetrahedralisation: it changes with the order of the input points and may change with the machine. Measured on the 47 benchmark masks with the default configuration: 9 row orders of the same tetrahedra gave 9 different meshes in the median case, and up to 0.78 degrees of line-mean contact-angle error and 3.8 points of tension error on one case; with the canonical order all 9 gave the same mesh, in 47 of 47 cases. False keeps Qhull's row order, which reproduces the meshes of dw3d 0.7 and earlier on the machine they were made on. Under the canonical order, between machines, remaining differences are expected only at exactly cospherical points (five or more points on one sphere, where Qhull's choice of tetrahedralisation itself may differ); this is confirmed on Linux x86-64 in continuous integration (Python 3.12 and 3.13).

True label_enclosed_media bool

Whether an enclosed pocket of label 0 (a lumen, a cavity: a 6-connected piece of label 0 touching no face of the array) becomes its own region, flagged as a medium, when its inscribed radius is at least the placement's min_distance + 1 voxels and two or more cells line it. Defaults to True since 0.7.1. Before, such a pocket had no watershed seed and the first cell its tetrahedra reached took all of it (measured on a 697-cell embryo: a 389 918-voxel lumen inside one cell, at 2.40 times the cell's voxel volume). The new labels are max + 1, ... in the order of each pocket's lowest raster index; enclosed_medium_report and medium_labels say which, the .rec file records them (media = ...), and EnclosedMediumWarning names the cell that took each pocket left (below the bound, lined by one cell). False leaves every pocket to the cells, as in 0.7.0. Independently of this switch, since 0.7.1 every piece of label 0 touching the image box gets its own label-0 seed, and a seed whose nearest tetrahedron lies outside its own label's voxels is moved to the nearest one inside (or dropped when there is none), so that no region is seeded in a neighbour. A mask with no pocket at or above the bound, one exterior piece and every seed already inside its label is reconstructed bitwise as before. See dw3d.enclosed_media.

True pad_thin_medium_margins bool

Whether a mask whose first mesh has a vertex on a face of the image box that no cell reaches is meshed again, padded with label 0 on every such face whose margin is below 2 * min_distance + 2 voxels, up to that margin; the mesh is returned in the mask's frame and medium_margin_padding says which faces were padded. Defaults to True since 0.8.0. Before, a cell a few voxels from the image box could take the medium between them (a 12-voxel cube with a margin of 4 voxels meshed to 2.98 times its voxel count, at min_distance 3). A mask whose first mesh has no such vertex is meshed bitwise as before. False reproduces 0.7's meshes. A cell left with triangles on a face its voxels do not reach (a face a cell reaches is never padded) is named by ThinMediumMarginWarning. See dw3d.thin_medium_margins. construct_mesh_in_physical_units does not pad a mask it resamples (voxels longer along one axis) unless asked to: see its pad_thin_medium_margins.

True

docs.title: last_compressed_segmentation property
docs.text:
last_compressed_segmentation: dict[str]

The last mesh's points and triangles, the watershed seeds and the mask's shape, as a dictionary.

Keys: points, triangles, seeds (one voxel index per label of the mask, label 0 included when present, in ascending label order) and image_shape. Save it with dw3d.save_compressed_segmentation (numpy.save). dw3d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict expects the points in voxel units of the mask, so read this before any scaling (set_pixel_size, set_global_min_max).

The frame of each entry:

  • points are the mesh's current points, last_constructed_mesh[0] itself: voxel indices of the meshed grid after construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask, but in physical units (the unit of spacing) after construct_mesh_in_physical_units, and as scaled by any later set_pixel_size, set_global_min_max or center_around_zero.
  • seeds and image_shape are always voxel indices and the shape of the grid that was meshed. After construct_mesh_in_physical_units that is the mask resampled to cubic voxels of resampled_spacing (the shortest spacing), not the mask that was passed in.

So after construct_mesh_in_physical_units the points are not in the frame of the seeds: divide them by resampled_spacing before dw3d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict, which then rebuilds the resampled cubic-grid mask. Passed as they are, the mesh is rasterised at the wrong scale (measured on a two-cell mask with spacing (0.6, 0.3, 0.3): 7 % of voxels agree with the resampled mask, against 96 % after the division).

docs.title: construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask
docs.text:
construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmented_image: NDArray[uint]) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.uint], NDArray[np.uint]]

Build a 3D mesh from a segmentation mask.

The mask is meshed on its own voxel grid, whatever its voxel size: for a mask whose voxels are longer along one axis, use construct_mesh_in_physical_units. The point placement's min_distance counts voxels of this grid.

After the call, last_constructed_mesh, crop_faces, cut_cells, crop_face_report, cell_volume_report, relocation_report and relocation_provenance describe this mesh, and save_to_rec_mesh writes no physical frame.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmented_image NDArray[uint]

the 3-D integer label mask; label 0 is the medium, every other label a cell.

required

Returns:

Type Description tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[uint], NDArray[uint]]

tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.uint], NDArray[np.uint]]: (points, triangles, labels). points is (n, 3) float64 in voxel units of the mask, in its index order: column i is the position along the mask's axis i, so (z, y, x) for a (z, y, x) stack, and the centre of voxel (i, j, k) is the point (i, j, k). triangles is (m, 3) vertex indices. labels is (m, 2): the two regions each triangle separates, smaller label first; the triangle's normal points out of the first into the second. These are the algorithm's own arrays, not copies.

Warns:

Type Description CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning

once, when junction relocation is on and the point placement's min_distance is 5 or more.

CellVolumeDisagreementWarning

once, when some cells' mesh volume disagrees with their voxel count (see cell_volume_report).

AbnormalEdgeWarning

once, when the finished mesh has abnormal non-manifold edges, with their number and the configuration.

UnresolvedCellWarning

once, when a label of the mask is absent from the finished mesh, whatever the cause, naming each such region (see enclosed_medium_report.unresolved). Since 0.8.0 this includes a cell too small to hold a tetrahedron, and a mask whose mesh has no triangle at all (it is returned empty, (0, 3) triangles); before, both raised AxisError.

ThinMediumMarginWarning

once, when a cell's mesh lies on a face of the image box that its voxels do not reach and that could not be padded (see pad_thin_medium_margins), naming each such cell, the face and its margin.

A mask whose first mesh has a vertex on an image face that no cell reaches is meshed a second time, padded with label 0 on the faces no cell reaches (pad_thin_medium_margins, medium_margin_padding); the mesh, the reports and last_compressed_segmentation are in the mask's frame either way.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for a mask that is neither 2-D nor 3-D, or a 3-D mask with an axis of length 1 (pass mask[0]); for a 2-D mask, a configuration with no 2-D meaning (see the class docstring).

ImportError

for a 2-D mask when dw2d is not installed (pip install delaunay-watershed).

docs.title: construct_mesh_in_physical_units
docs.text:
construct_mesh_in_physical_units(segmented_image: NDArray[uint], spacing: tuple[float, float, float], *, resampling: str = 'shape', spacing_unit: str | None = None, axis_order: str = 'zyx', pad_thin_medium_margins: bool | None = None) -> tuple[NDArray[np.float64], NDArray[np.uint], NDArray[np.uint]]

Build a mesh, in physical units, from a mask whose voxels may be longer along one axis.

The mask is first resampled to cubic voxels of the shortest spacing by dw3d.mask_preprocessing.resample_to_isotropic (shape-based interpolation by default), then meshed by construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask with this algorithm's settings unchanged (min_distance counts voxels of the resampled cubic grid), and the mesh is scaled to physical units: a point at voxel index i of the cubic grid is at i * h, h = min(spacing), so the centre of the mask's first voxel is the origin. The columns stay in the mask's index order, (z, y, x) for a (z, y, x) stack.

Why resample rather than mesh the native grid and scale it: measured on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells at a real cell size, down-sampled along z, against the same tissues meshed at full resolution, meshing the native grid costs +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 degrees of contact-angle error at k = 5/3, 2 and 3 (k = long spacing / short spacing), and resampling first +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17 (on dw3d 0.7.0's meshes, before 0.8.0 pads thin margins of medium on the native grid; not measured again); see dw3d.mask_preprocessing. The cost is that of a mask acquired at the short spacing: k times the voxels.

The reports (crop_faces, cut_cells, crop_face_report, cell_volume_report, relocation_report) describe the mesh on the resampled cubic grid, in its voxel units, before the scaling.

After this call save_to_rec_mesh writes, in the file's metadata appendix, coordinate_frame = physical, axis_order, spacing (the mask's own voxel size, which the mesh coordinates are already scaled by), spacing_unit when given, source_shape, resampling and resampled_spacing. Any later reconstruction clears them. Do not call set_pixel_size on the result: it is already in physical units.

last_compressed_segmentation then holds the physical points with the seeds and the shape of the resampled cubic grid: divide its points by resampled_spacing before dw3d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict (see that property).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default segmented_image NDArray[uint]

the 3-D integer label mask; label 0 is the medium.

required spacing tuple[float, float, float]

voxel size along the mask's axes 0, 1, 2, so (dz, dy, dx) for a (z, y, x) stack, in any one unit. One axis may be coarser than the other two, which must be equal (to a relative tolerance of 1e-6).

required resampling str

"shape" (default) or "nearest"; see dw3d.mask_preprocessing.

'shape' spacing_unit str | None

the unit of spacing (e.g. "um"), recorded, not used.

None axis_order str

what the mask's axes are, recorded, not used. Defaults to "zyx".

'zyx' pad_thin_medium_margins bool | None

whether thin medium margins are padded (see the class's option of that name), for this call only. None (default): this algorithm's setting for cubic voxels, and off for a mask that is resampled (voxels longer along one axis). Measured on a four-cell ball with voxels twice as long along z, over dither seeds 42-141: with the padding a cell kept less than half its voxel volume on 20 of 100 seeds, without it on 3 of 100 (McNemar exact p = 1.5e-5; on cubic voxels 13 against 10, p = 0.51); the cell is lost in the watershed, by a mechanism not yet found. Unpadded, a cell a few voxels from a face of the image box may take the medium between them, and ThinMediumMarginWarning names it. For a 2-D mask, None keeps this algorithm's setting.

None

Returns:

Name Type Description tuple tuple[NDArray[float64], NDArray[uint], NDArray[uint]]

(points, triangles, labels) as construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask returns them, the points in the unit of spacing. For cubic voxels of size 1 they are bitwise those of construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmented_image).

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

for a spacing that is not three positive finite numbers or has two different fine axes, an unknown resampling method, or a mask that is not 3-D.

Warns:

Type Description UnmeasuredAnisotropyWarning

when the voxels are more than MEASURED_ANISOTROPY_RATIO_MAX (3) times longer along one axis, a range in which the accuracy was not measured. The mesh is built anyway.

CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning

as in construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask.

CellVolumeDisagreementWarning

as in construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask.

AbnormalEdgeWarning

as in construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask.

docs.title: Thin margins of medium
docs.text: A thin margin of medium between a cell and the image box: why the cell took it, and the padding that prevents it.

docs.title: The defect
docs.text:
Before 0.8.0, a cell separated from a face of the image box by a few voxels of medium could take that medium: at the default min_distance of 3, a 12-voxel cube 4 voxels from every face meshed to 2.98 times its voxel count, and the two boxes of a 24-voxel smoke mask to 2.46 times. The mechanism, measured on cubes of side 8 to 32:

  1. The distance field is 0 on the image box's outer layer of voxels (dw3d.edt._pad_mask makes the box a boundary), which is below the level of the membranes (M - 1, 0.732 on these masks).
  2. A minimum is placed only where no lower voxel lies within min_distance (skimage.feature.peak_local_max's window). So the membrane between the cell and a face loses its minima to the box: at a margin of 2 or 3 voxels it carries none at all, on every cube measured.
  3. With no point on that membrane, the tetrahedra joining the cell's interior point to the box span the medium, and the seeded watershed hands them to the cell through faces scoring like the cell's interior. Even a labelling by tetrahedron centroid would give the cell 1.26 to 1.47 times its voxels: the tetrahedralisation is wrong there, not only its labelling.

The range grows with min_distance: the defect reached margins of 5 to 7 voxels at min_distance 3, 7 to 8 at 4 and 8 to 10 at 5, and was gone from 2 * min_distance + 2 voxels on (8, 10, 12), on cubes of side 12 to 32. Its signature was exact on those cubes: every cube whose mesh volume exceeded its voxel count by more than 15 % had triangles of the cell on a face of the image box that the cell's voxels do not reach (unsupported border triangles). Real cells are rounded and come close to the box at one place only; of 684 masks (47 benchmark tissues, 141 of the resolution sweep, 492 frames of a real embryo series, the four test images), 6 had unsupported border triangles (1 to 5 each), and the 362 cells within 7 voxels of a face kept a mesh volume of 0.85 to 1.45 times their voxel count, inside the agreement band of dw3d.cell_volume_agreement.

docs.title: The fix
docs.text:
needs_padding decides it after mesh surgery, before anything is reported: when a vertex of the mesh lies on a face of the image box that no cell of the mask reaches, the reconstruction is run again on the mask padded with label 0 on every face that no cell reaches and whose margin (its smallest gap to a cell) is below thin_margin_bound(min_distance), each up to that bound (padding_of_thin_margins), and the finished mesh is translated back into the mask's frame. Every cell then sits at least 2 * min_distance + 2 voxels from those faces, as on a mask imaged with a wider margin. The mask's own voxels keep the dither they have unpadded (the default placement adds U(0, 1e-5) from RandomState(42) to the distance field; drawn on the padded array, every voxel would get another value, and the whole mesh would be a new draw): dither_padding of dw3d.points_on_edt._dithered. So only the mesh within the padded faces' reach changes: on the 18 padded masks of the lab's data, 0 to 28 line-mean wedges of 3 to 123 changed on 13 resolution-sweep masks and 4 to 18 of about 700 on 5 embryo frames, where a dither drawn on the padded array changed every wedge. All thin faces are padded, not only the one that triggered: the tetrahedralisation is global, and padding one face of a cube 4 voxels from every face moved the defect to the others (1.13 to 2.68 times the voxel count). A mask whose first mesh has no vertex on a face no cell reaches is meshed exactly as before. A face that a cell reaches is a crop (dw3d.crop_faces) and is never padded: padding it with medium would close the cut cells there. A cell left with unsupported border triangles, on such a face or on a face whose margin is already at the bound, is named by ThinMediumMarginWarning.

On a padded face the mesh is that of the same tissue imaged with a wider margin, so the cell's surface may reach a few voxels into the medium there, and past the image box when the margin is thinner than that reach; before, the box clipped it and the cell took the medium instead. The overshoot is at most the face's padding (the mesh lies inside the padded box), and was measured at: 7 voxels on a 16-voxel cube 1 voxel from every face, and up to 4 on cubes of side 8 to 24 at margins of 1 to 5 voxels; up to 4 voxels on foambryo's test masks (four cells in a ball 4 voxels from the faces, with cubic voxels); 0 to 2 voxels on the 18 padded masks of the lab's data (one vertex by 1 voxel on one resolution-sweep mask, five vertices by up to 2 voxels on one embryo frame, none on the others). No vertex passes a crop face, which is never padded.

What the padding does not do: it does not change how the watershed treats small cells. On a ball of four cells cut by the image box, at min_distance 3, the cell that the watershed empties (UnresolvedCellWarning, cause "removed by mesh surgery") is kept only as a fragment of 4 triangles, 0.010 of its voxel volume inside the box of voxel centres; and a cell with one or two interior points (a cube of 8 or 12 voxels, or a cell of that ball) can fall below half its voxel count on some dither draws, with or without padding (2 of 20 seeds for the 8-voxel cube 8 voxels from every face).

Where it is not applied by default: a mask that construct_mesh_in_physical_units resamples (voxels longer along one axis). On foambryo's four-cell ball 4 voxels from the faces, with z twice as long, over dither seeds 42-141, a cell kept less than half its voxel volume on 20 of 100 seeds padded against 3 of 100 unpadded (McNemar exact p = 1.5e-5; with cubic voxels 13 against 10, p = 0.51). The cell is lost in the watershed: the cell facing a padded face hands most of its interior to the medium through a face straddling its outer membrane, before that interior reaches its seed; the distance field there is the unpadded one, the tetrahedralisation near the padded faces is not, and why this happens more often on resampled masks was not found. Such a mask keeps 0.7's thin-margin meshes, named by ThinMediumMarginWarning; pad_thin_medium_margins=True in that call pads it.

What the trigger misses: it reads the first mesh's vertices, so a cell that collapses near a face without reaching it is not padded. On cubes of side 6 to 12 voxels 1 to 5 voxels from one or every face, min_distance 3 to 5, ten dither seeds (1 200 runs), 25 collapsed to 0.00-0.49 of their voxels with no vertex on a face; padded, they give 0.58-0.80, and the same cubes 16 voxels from every face 0.51-0.71. dw2d decides from the mask instead (dw2d.thin_medium_margins).

docs.title: ThinMediumMarginWarning
docs.text:
Bases: UserWarning

A cell's mesh lies on a face of the image box that its voxels do not reach, and padding could not prevent it.

Emitted once per reconstruction, naming each such cell, the face, the cell's medium margin to it (the number of voxels of label 0 between the cell and the face) and why the face was not padded: a cell reaches it (it is a crop), padding is switched off, or the margin is already thin_margin_bound(min_distance) or more. The cell may have taken some of the medium between it and the face; compare its volume with its voxel count (cell_volume_report). See dw3d.thin_medium_margins.

docs.title: Self-intersections
docs.text:
Exact nonlocal triangle-triangle intersection for a surface mesh.

Two triangles that share a vertex index are adjacent and are never tested: adjacent triangles touch by construction, and in a correct multimaterial mesh three triangles meet along every trijunction edge, so counting those would report the intended non-manifold structure as a defect. Every other pair is nonlocal and is tested exactly.

docs.title: Why the library carries this and not only the benchmarks
docs.text:
Every other validity property a mesh consumer can check cheaply is local or combinatorial: watertightness, non-manifold edges, degenerate and duplicate faces, interface identity. A mesh whose two distant sheets pass through each other satisfies all of them. Measured on this package's own benchmark cohort: all twelve local predicates stayed bit-identical on 40 of 40 cases while 23 nonlocal crossings existed on 5 of them, introduced by a post-process whose guard checked only the triangles incident to the vertex it moved.

A local guard cannot certify a nonlocal property. :mod:dw3d.junction_relocation therefore uses this predicate as its own acceptance test, which is why the predicate belongs to the library rather than to a benchmark package the library must not depend on.

docs.title: The test
docs.text:
For each candidate pair, the exact Moller triangle-triangle predicate:

  1. Signed distances of triangle B's vertices to triangle A's plane. If all three carry the same strict sign, that plane separates them and they cannot meet.
  2. The same with the roles exchanged.
  3. If either triangle is coplanar with the other's plane, fall back to a 2-D test in that plane: any edge-edge crossing, or either triangle's vertex inside the other.
  4. Otherwise both triangles cross the line where the two planes meet. Each cuts an interval on that line, and the triangles meet iff the two intervals overlap.

Steps 1, 2 and 4 are the standard construction and are exact up to floating point. The predicate is checked against an independent Moller-Trumbore segment-triangle oracle that shares no arithmetic with it, over random pairs; that differential test lives beside the benchmark evaluator.

docs.title: Complexity
docs.text: Candidate pairs come from a cKDTree on triangle centroids queried at twice the largest circumradius about the centroid. That bound is sound: two triangles whose centroids are further apart than the sum of their circumradii cannot meet, and twice the largest circumradius is at least that sum. The exact predicate then runs vectorised over the candidate set.

docs.title: Units, tolerances and failure modes
docs.text:
Coordinates are the mesh's own units -- mask voxels for a reconstruction read in the mask frame -- and all arithmetic is float64. :data:CONTACT_TOLERANCE is an absolute distance in those units: a pair whose contact is within it is reported as touching rather than counted as an intersection, and both numbers are emitted so a borderline pair cannot hide inside a single total. A degenerate triangle has no well-defined plane; such triangles are excluded from the test and counted separately, because silently skipping one would let a sliver hide a crossing. A mesh with fewer than two triangles returns zero counts.

A self-intersection is not affine-invariant in general, so a mesh and its registered copy are two different meshes for this predicate and must be reported as such.

The count is a count, never a score, and no threshold is proposed here or anywhere else.

No new dependency: numpy and scipy only, both already required.
