docs.title: The Polyscope viewer
docs.text:
Optional Polyscope viewer for a reconstructed mesh, for inspection and debugging.

Install it with the viewing extra (pip install "delaunay-watershed-3d[viewing]"), which brings Polyscope and matplotlib. Calling the viewer opens a Polyscope window.

The window draws the tissue, not its mirror image. The mesh's points are in the mask's index order, (z, y, x) for a microscope stack, and Polyscope reads the columns it is handed as its own (x, y, z). The viewer hands it the columns reversed, (x, y, z) = columns (2, 1, 0), the mask's column, row and slice, and each triangle (a, b, c) as (a, c, b), so that it still faces the same side (_drawn_points, _drawn_triangles). Exchanging two axes is a reflection, which reverses every triangle's orientation; reversing the triangles undoes that. Up to 0.7.0 the columns were handed as they are: every view was the mirror image of the tissue. Only what is drawn is reordered; the stored mesh and the files written (.rec, .vtk) keep the mask's order.

A 2-D mesh (dw2d's (points (n, 2), segments (m, 2), labels (m, 2)), or the algorithm after a 2-D mask) is drawn in a 2-D window by the same function. Each cell's boundary, the 2-D counterpart of the closed surface the 3-D view draws for it, is one curve network in the cell's colour, the colour the 3-D view gives the same label (the same generator, seeded as there). The cells are not filled: no polygon triangulation is needed, and none is done. Polyscope's (x, y) is the mesh's (column, -row) (_drawn_planar_points): a quarter-turn rotation, not a reflection, so the window shows the image as napari and matplotlib's imshow do, row 0 at the top and column 0 at the left. The camera looks straight down on the plane, with planar navigation (pan and zoom, no rotation), restored to the previous style when the function returns. An image or a mask given as image is drawn under the curves, one texel per pixel, pixel (row, column) centred on the mesh point (row, column) (times the pixel size of a mesh built in physical units).

Matthieu Perez, 2024.

docs.title: plot_cells_polyscope
docs.text:
plot_cells_polyscope(reconstruct: MeshReconstructionAlgorithm | tuple[NDArray, NDArray, NDArray], anisotropy_factor: float = 1.0, clean_before: bool = True, clean_after: bool = True, transparency: bool = False, show: bool = True, view: str = 'Simple', scattering_coeff: float = 0.5, *, image: NDArray | None = None) -> None

Plot separated cells of the mesh in a polyscope viewer, in 3D or in 2D: the mesh decides.

Each cell (every label but the medium 0) is shown as its own surface, in a random colour (fixed seed). Polyscope's x, y, z are the mask's column, row and slice (the points' columns 2, 1, 0): the tissue is drawn as it is, not its mirror image (see the module's docstring).

A 2-D mesh (points (n, 2), (row, column)) opens a 2-D window instead: each cell's boundary as a curve network in the colour the 3-D view gives that label, (x, y) = (column, -row) (rows downward, as in napari and matplotlib), a camera straight down, image under the curves when given (the module's docstring).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default reconstruct MeshReconstructionAlgorithm | tuple

the algorithm whose last constructed mesh to show (dw3d's, after a 3-D or a 2-D mask, or dw2d's), or a mesh as three arrays: (points, triangles, labels) in 3D, dw2d's (points, segments, labels) in 2D.

required anisotropy_factor float

Multiply column 0 of the points, the mask's axis 0 (z for a (z, y, x) stack), by this factor, for display only: a scaled copy is shown, and the reconstruction's own mesh is left unchanged. Defaults to 1.0. To build a mesh in physical units from a mask whose voxels are longer along z, use MeshReconstructionAlgorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units instead. 3D only: 2-D meshes have square pixels, and any other value raises ValueError for a 2-D mesh.

1.0 clean_before bool

Clean viewer before the function. Defaults to True.

True clean_after bool

Clean viewer after the function. Defaults to True.

True transparency bool

Allow transparency in viewer. Defaults to False.

False show bool

Show viewer. Defaults to True.

True view str

"Simple" or "Scattered", scatter different cells or not. Defaults to "Simple".

'Simple' scattering_coeff float

If "Scattered" mode, Coefficient of scattering. Defaults to 0.5.

0.5 image NDArray | None

2D only: an image drawn under the mesh, on the mask's pixel grid: (rows, columns) grey (scaled between its 0.5 % and 99.5 % quantiles; a label mask is drawn this way too) or (rows, columns, 3 or 4) RGB(A) (floats in [0, 1] or integers in [0, 255]). Not drawn in the scattered view. Defaults to None. Keyword-only.

None

Raises:

Type Description ImportError

if Polyscope is not installed (the viewing extra).

ValueError

for an option that has no meaning in the mesh's dimension (anisotropy_factor other than 1 with a 2-D mesh, image with a 3-D mesh), an image that is neither grey nor RGB(A), an unknown view, or a mesh whose points are neither (n, 3) nor (n, 2).

docs.title: Migrating from dw2d 0.1.5
docs.text:
delaunay-watershed-2d 0.1.5 was the last release of dw2d from its own repository. From 0.8.0 dw2d is developed and released with dw3d, under one version. Code written for 0.1.5 still runs through 0.8.x, with deprecation warnings, but its meshes and some of its numbers change: this page lists what changes and how to get the former behaviour back.

If you use dw2d, please cite: Yamamoto K., Ichbiah S., Perez M., Borrego-Pinto J., Delbary F., Goehring N. W., Northrop P., Turlier H., Charras G. Spatiotemporal mapping of the contractile and adhesive forces sculpting early C. elegans embryos. Developmental Cell 61(6), 1273–1288.e4 (2026), doi:10.1016/j.devcel.2026.04.013.

docs.title: Installation and licence
docs.text:
pip install delaunay-watershed            # dw3d and dw2d
pip install delaunay-watershed-2d         # dw2d alone, as before

pip install --upgrade delaunay-watershed-2d replaces 0.1.5 in place. The import is unchanged (import dw2d). dw2d 0.8.0 needs Python 3.12 or later, NumPy 2.0, SciPy 1.13 (it runs on SciPy 1.14 and later, which removed interp2d), scikit-image 0.23.1, networkx 2.8 and iorec 1.4.1; matplotlib only for figures (pip install "delaunay-watershed-2d[viewing]"), and no longer Polyscope. dw2d is licensed under GPL-3.0-or-later from 0.8.0, like dw3d; 0.1.5 and earlier keep the licence they were published under.

docs.title: The new names
docs.text:
The 0.1.5 call and its 0.8.0 equivalent:

# 0.1.5 (still works through 0.8.x, with a DeprecationWarning)
from dw2d import geometry_reconstruction_2d
DW = geometry_reconstruction_2d(labels, min_dist=4, expansion_labels=0)
verts, edges = DW.return_mesh()           # edges: (m, 4) [v1, v2, m1, m2]
mesh = DW.return_dcel()
DW.export_mesh("mesh.rec", mode="txt")
DW.export_segmentation("compressed.npy")

# 0.8.0
import dw2d
algorithm = dw2d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm(min_distance=4)
points, segments, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(labels_image)
mesh = algorithm.last_constructed_dcel
algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh("mesh.rec")
dw2d.save_compressed_segmentation("compressed.npy", algorithm.last_compressed_segmentation)
0.1.5 0.8.0 geometry_reconstruction_2d(labels, min_dist=…, expansion_labels=…, interpolation_points=…) get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm(min_distance=…), or the factory's set_peak_local_points_placement_method, set_label_expansion, set_score_samples deterministic= (development versions only) set_canonical_triangle_order / canonical_triangle_order relocate_junctions=, project_interface_vertices=, repair_pinch_vertices=, relabel_near_tie_slivers= (development versions only) set_junction_relocation, set_interface_projection, set_pinch_vertex_repair, set_near_tie_sliver_relabelling DW.return_mesh() → (verts, edges), edges (m, 4) construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask) → (points, segments, labels), as dw3d DW.return_dcel() algorithm.last_constructed_dcel DW.export_mesh(filename, mode) algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh(filename, binary_mode=False) DW.export_segmentation(filename) algorithm.last_compressed_segmentation, dw2d.save_compressed_segmentation reconstruct_mask_from_dict(filename) reconstruct_mask_from_dict(dictionary), reconstruct_mask_from_saved_file_dict(filename) read_rec_file_bin, read_rec_file_num, open_mesh_multitracker (in dw2d.Dcel) dw2d.io.load_rec(filename) → (points, segments, labels) write_mesh_bin, write_mesh_text (in dw2d.Dcel) dw2d.io.save_rec(filename, points, segments, labels, binary_mode=False) DW.simple_plot(), DW.plot_polylines_and_seeds() the same methods on the algorithm, or dw3d.viewing.plot_cells_polyscope(algorithm, image=mask) relocation and projection functions returning a dictionary relocate_junction_vertices(mask, points, segments, labels, ...), project_interface_vertices(mask, points, segments, labels, ...), returning JunctionRelocationReport and InterfaceProjectionReport

Deprecated names, kept through 0.8.x and removed in 0.9. geometry_reconstruction_2d (with min_dist, return_mesh, return_dcel, export_mesh, export_segmentation and its plotting methods) warns once, when constructed, and computes exactly as before. The .rec readers and writers of 0.1.5 call the new functions, return what they returned before and warn. Every other name 0.1.5 exported from its top level (the half-edge and plotting helpers of dw2d.Dcel, trace_line, Delaunay_Graph, seeded_watershed_map, the helpers of dw2d.Plotting_tools, …) still resolves, with a DeprecationWarning naming its module. reconstruct_mask_from_dict given a file name warns and reads the file. The third-party names that 0.1.5's star imports leaked (dw2d.np, dw2d.plt, dw2d.pickle, …) are gone; import them yourself. open_mesh_multitracker no longer has a default file name and detects the layout itself. export_mesh with a mode other than 'bin' or 'txt' raises ValueError (it printed a message and wrote nothing).

docs.title: Defaults that change results
docs.text:
Every one of these changes the mesh of some masks; each is on in 0.8.0, and each can be turned off. Their measured effects are in the 2D user guide.

default what changes how to turn it off a machine-independent route (canonical triangle order) cells of four or more cocircular points are triangulated by a fixed rule: 2 of the 18 golden cases change, by about 0.05 % of one interface length set_canonical_triangle_order(False) junction relocation every junction vertex moves onto the mask's own junction, by a fraction of a pixel set_junction_relocation(False) pinch-vertex repair a few triangles are relabelled where a cell or a material was split around one vertex; meshes whose half-edge structure 0.1.5 could not build now build set_pinch_vertex_repair(False) near-tie sliver relabelling on the route without relocation, Z-shaped folds along membranes are removed; off with relocation, so off by default set_near_tie_sliver_relabelling(False) image-border vertices marked the vertices on the image border are never moved by the relocation or the projection; 7 of 972 border junctions on 82 test meshes stay on the border instead of moving inside the image (always on) thin margins of medium padded a cell a few pixels from a side no cell reaches no longer takes the margin; none of the shipped masks is padded pad_thin_medium_margins = False

0.1.5's mesh, as nearly as it can be had:

algorithm = (
    dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory()
    .set_canonical_triangle_order(False)
    .set_junction_relocation(False)
    .set_pinch_vertex_repair(False)
    .set_near_tie_sliver_relabelling(False)
    .make_algorithm()
)
algorithm.pad_thin_medium_margins = False

Its vertices are 0.1.5's on the same machine (the legacy triangulation of cocircular points depends on the machine, as it did), and its edges are stored in the 0.8.0 orientation (below).

One shipped mask, data/two_dimensional/Masks/mask_Cells_2.tif (157 × 173 pixels, 50 cells), its labels expanded by 6 pixels (set_label_expansion(6)) so that the cells touch, at min_distance 4 pixels: the route of 0.1.5 (left, grey) and the 0.8.0 defaults (right, black), each drawn over the mask (cells grey, medium white), with the junction vertices (red) and the image-border vertices (blue). Both meshes have 431 vertices and 480 edges; the 0.8.0 defaults move 63 of the 95 junction vertices onto the mask's own junctions (median move 0.71 px), and the 368 other vertices are at the same positions. Made with delaunay-watershed 0.8.0 by docs/two_dimensional/figures/make_the_two_dimensional_figures.py.

docs.title: Fixes that change numbers
docs.text:
• compute_lengths and compute_curvatures were wrong on most interfaces. Where the half-edge structure reversed a material's boundary loop, it reversed the order of the loop's half-edges but not their endpoints, so walking such a face cut every interface one edge off its junctions, and a closed loop without junction lost its last edge. Over the shipped masks (2 080 interfaces that change) the former lengths were off by a median 7.4 %, and by more than a factor 2 on 50 short interfaces (2 to 17 px). compute_lengths is now the sum of each interface's edge lengths; compute_curvatures changes on the cell–cell interfaces, whose ends are now the junctions, and on closed loops without junction it now reads every vertex (228 of 228 such interfaces were off, by a median 3.5 %, at most 20 %). The mesh, compute_angles and compute_area_faces are unchanged. Recompute any length or curvature, and anything derived from them, obtained with 0.1.5.
  • The edges along the image border are oriented like every other edge (they came in an arbitrary order); the lengths of the medium interfaces of meshes with a cut cell change accordingly.
  • The mask rebuild (reconstruct_mask_from_dict) no longer loops for ever on a mesh whose vertices are off the pixel lattice, as they are after junction relocation.
  • A mask whose mesh has no edge returns an empty mesh and names its cells (UnresolvedCellWarning) instead of raising IndexError.

docs.title: The orientation of the edges
docs.text: 0.8.0 stores every edge the other way round: in [v1, v2, m1, m2] (or segments[k], labels[k]), m1 now lies on the left of v1 -> v2 in the mask's (row, column) frame; it lay on the right (on the left in (x, y) = (column, row)) in 0.1.5. Each edge is thus the positively oriented boundary of its first label, which is dw3d's rule for triangles: one rule in both dimensions (orientation). Only the order of the two vertices within each edge changes; no vertex, edge, label or edge order does, and the half-edge quantities (angles, lengths, curvatures, areas) are not affected by it. Code that reads an edge's direction changes sign: dw2d.Dcel.compute_areas, the signed area of each material from its oriented edges, now gives each cell a positive area (negative before). A .rec file written by 0.8.0 records the rule (orientation = boundary_of_first_label); files written by 0.1.5 do not. foambryo 0.8.0 measures each 2-D mesh's orientation and gives the same tensions and pressures from a mesh in either orientation.

docs.title: Files
docs.text: .rec files written by 0.1.5 read to the same arrays with dw2d.io.load_rec (and with the deprecated readers). Text files written by 0.8.0 hold every coordinate exactly (the shortest text that reads back to the same float64), where 0.1.5 rounded them to 5 decimals; the binary layout is unchanged, byte for byte. Every file written by save_to_rec_mesh (dw2d's algorithm, or dw3d's given a 2-D mask) carries an appendix that records dimension = 2 and the orientation rule; dw2d.io.save_rec writes one only when given metadata, and the deprecated export_mesh writes none, so dw3d.io.rec_dimension then tells the dimension from the file's layout.

docs.title: Two-dimensional masks
docs.text:
dw2d (distribution delaunay-watershed-2d) does in 2D what dw3d does in 3D: from a 2-D instance segmentation (an integer label image, 0 for the medium), it builds a multimaterial polygonal mesh, one polygonal line per interface between two cells or between a cell and the medium. The method is the same: points are placed on the ridges of the distance map to the cell boundaries, they are triangulated (Delaunay), and a seeded watershed on the triangulation's dual graph gives each triangle a label; the mesh is the set of edges between triangles of different labels. dw2d also builds a half-edge structure of that mesh, from which interface lengths, junction angles, curvatures and cell areas are read.

Since 0.8.0 the two packages are one experience: dw3d's algorithm given a 2-D mask hands it to dw2d, dw2d offers dw3d's names, both write .rec files that record their dimension, and dw3d's Polyscope viewer draws either. The input decides the dimension.

The mesh of the repository's mask data/two_dimensional/Masks/mask_Cells_3.tif (182 × 190 pixels, three cells), at the default min_distance 4 pixels with every 0.8.0 default, drawn over the mask (cells grey, medium white): each interface a polygonal line (black), its vertices (dots) and the junction vertices, moved onto the mask's own junctions (red). No cell reaches the image border here, so no edge of the mesh lies on it (the border points dw2d marks, image_border_vertices, belong to no segment). Made with delaunay-watershed 0.8.0 by docs/two_dimensional/figures/make_the_two_dimensional_figures.py.

docs.title: A first 2-D mesh
docs.text:
import tifffile
import dw2d

mask = tifffile.imread("data/two_dimensional/Masks/mask_Cells_3.tif")
algorithm = dw2d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()          # min_distance=4 pixels
points, segments, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask)
mesh = algorithm.last_constructed_dcel                                # the half-edge structure
lengths, angles = mesh.compute_lengths(), mesh.compute_angles()
algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh("mesh_2d.rec")

dw3d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm().construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask) gives the same arrays, bit for bit.

docs.title: The output
docs.text:
• points, (n, 2) float64: the vertices, in the mask's index order (row, column), in pixels (the centre of pixel (i, j) is the point (i, j)), or in the unit of the pixel size with construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing=(h, h)) (square pixels only);
  • segments, (m, 2) int64: indices into points;
  • labels, (m, 2) int64: the two materials each edge separates, smaller first. The first label lies on the left of each edge segments[k, 0] -> segments[k, 1] in (row, column): each edge is the positively oriented boundary of its first label, the rule dw3d's triangles follow too (orientation).

docs.title: Where to go next
docs.text:
• Reconstruction in 2D: every option, its 0.8.0 default and what it was measured to change; the image border and cropped masks; lengths, angles and curvatures.
  • Migrating from dw2d 0.1.5: the install, the defaults that change results, the fixes, the orientation, the deprecated names.
  • Thin margins of medium: the padding of thin margins, in 2D and 3D.
  • The notebooks: geometrical analysis, compressing a tissue and compressing separated cells.
  • The API: the dw2d package and its modules.

foambryo infers the tensions and pressures of a 2-D tissue from these meshes, with the same calls as in 3D.

docs.title: Building the algorithm
docs.text:
dw2d.get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm(min_distance=4, print_info=False) returns the default algorithm. dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory builds another one step by step, with dw3d's names where the step has a 2-D meaning; each set_* method returns the factory, and make_algorithm() builds the algorithm:

import dw2d

algorithm = (
    dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory()
    .set_peak_local_points_placement_method(min_distance=3)
    .set_junction_relocation(True)
    .set_interface_projection(True)
    .make_algorithm()
)

Every option is also an attribute of the algorithm (algorithm.relocate_junctions = False) and a keyword of dw2d.MeshReconstructionAlgorithm(...). One algorithm meshes any number of masks; its reports describe the last one.

dw3d's algorithm given a 2-D mask configures dw2d from its own settings that have a 2-D meaning (min_distance, junction relocation, canonical order, pad_thin_medium_margins, print_info); a dw3d configuration without a 2-D meaning (boundary-layer, junction-protected or link-checked placement, another distance transform, tessellation or face score, physical image faces, mesh surgery off) raises ValueError naming it. dw2d places its points without a random dither, so dw3d's default (dithered) and deterministic configurations mesh a 2-D mask alike.

docs.title: The options and their defaults
docs.text:
Measured effects are on synthetic two-dimensional foams at mechanical equilibrium with known tensions and pressures (53 held-out tissues of 4 to 64 cells, 661 images: exact masks, crops and smooth boundary noise of 0.5 to 2 px, with cells of 10, 20 and 40 px radius), read by foambryo's circular-arc angle reading unless stated otherwise.

option (factory setter; attribute) default what it does, and what it was measured to change set_peak_local_points_placement_method(min_distance); min_distance 4 pixels The minimum distance between the triangulation's points, in pixels (dw3d: 3 voxels). Smaller gives a finer, slower mesh. set_canonical_triangle_order; canonical_triangle_order on (new in 0.8.0) Makes the mesh the same on every machine. Where four or more points lie on one circle (frequent, since they are integer pixels), the Delaunay triangulation is not unique and Qhull picks differently on Linux x86-64 and macOS arm64; such cells are triangulated by a fixed rule, triangles and graph edges are listed in a canonical order, and the watershed sorts stably. Against dw2d 0.1.5, 2 of the 18 golden cases change (one interface length by about 0.05 %, no angle). False keeps the legacy route. dw3d's analogue is canonical_tetrahedron_order. set_junction_relocation; relocate_junctions on (since 0.8.0) Moves every junction vertex with an unambiguous counterpart onto the corner where three labels meet between pixels, connectivity frozen, under guards against edge crossings and contacts. The junctions move from 0.65 to 0.42 px of the true ones (medians), the junction-angle error falls by 0.85° (95 % interval 0.75 to 0.95) and the relative tension error by 0.007 (0.004 to 0.010); better or not resolved in 13 of 14 tiers, including boundary noise of 0.75 px, the level measured on real 2D masks, and worse in one (0.5 px of noise with 40 px cells: +0.007, interval 0.000 to 0.012). Read with chords instead, it lowers the angle error by about 1.8° and the tension error by about 0.025. relocation_report says what moved. set_interface_projection; interface_projection off With junction relocation, then moves every interface vertex onto its label pair's interface in the mask; together the two lower the angle error by about 2.5°. Alone it made the error worse, so requesting it without relocation raises ValueError. interface_projection_report says what moved. set_pinch_vertex_repair; pinch_vertex_repair on (new in 0.8.0) Repairs a cell left in two pieces, or a material in two sectors around one vertex, by relabelling a few triangles (no point moves), so that the half-edge structure of tissue masks can be built. Where nothing needs repairing the mesh is unchanged (every golden case; 14 of 24 shipped-mask settings); on the other 10, building the half-edge structure used to fail and now succeeds. set_near_tie_sliver_relabelling; near_tie_sliver_relabelling None: on without junction relocation, off with it Gives a flat membrane triangle its flat neighbour's label where the watershed's choice between them was a near tie (within 0.1 px of edge score) and the change removes a Z-shaped fold of the interface. On the plain mesh (159 images, min_distance 3) it removes every such fold, leaves the chord angles unchanged and makes the pressures more accurate by a median 0.0026 of the RMS true pressure (0.0013 to 0.0053); after relocation the gain was not distinguishable from zero, hence off there unless True. False turns it off everywhere. pad_thin_medium_margins on (new in 0.8.0) Pads with medium every side of the image that no cell reaches and whose margin is below 2 * min_distance + 2 pixels, before meshing; see thin margins of medium. medium_margin_padding says which sides were padded. set_label_expansion(pixels); label_expansion 0 Grows the labels by this many pixels before meshing (skimage.segmentation.expand_labels), for masks whose cells do not touch. set_score_samples(n); score_samples 10 The number of points sampled along each triangle edge to score it on the distance map.

dw2d 0.1.5's mesh is the one built with canonical_triangle_order=False, relocate_junctions=False, pinch_vertex_repair=False, near_tie_sliver_relabelling=False, pad_thin_medium_margins=False, except that its edges were stored in the opposite orientation (migration).

docs.title: The image border and cropped masks
docs.text:
A cell that reaches the image border is cut by it. dw2d closes it there with edges along the border, whose other material is the medium (label 0), and marks the vertices on the border:

  • algorithm.image_border_vertices: the indices of the vertices on the image border, taken from the triangulation before any vertex moves (the endpoints of its hull edges, which run along the border because the image's four corners are triangulated with the points); the junction relocation and the interface projection never move them. The half-edge structure carries them as DCEL_Data.image_border_vertices, and the compressed segmentation and the .rec appendix keep them.
  • algorithm.cut_cells: the cells with a vertex on the image border.

foambryo uses the mark to leave the junctions on the image border out of its 2-D inference, whose wedge in the medium is the image's cut, not a membrane. Before 0.8.0, where the mask had medium pixels on the border next to two cells, the junction relocation moved the junction there 0.7 to 2.9 px inside the image (7 of 972 border junctions on 82 test meshes); it now stays on the border.

The edges along the border are oriented like every other edge (before 0.8.0 they came in an arbitrary order, 164 of 165 reversed on one shipped mask), so each material's edges run around it in one sense.

docs.title: Lengths, angles, curvatures, areas
docs.text:
algorithm.last_constructed_dcel (or dw2d.DCEL_Data(points, edges), with edges the (m, 4) array [v1, v2, m1, m2]) is a half-edge structure:

  • compute_lengths(): a dictionary, interface (a, b) → its length in pixels (or the mesh's unit), the sum of its edges' lengths;
  • compute_angles(): the angle of each material at each junction, in radians, keyed (a, b, c): the angle inside material b between its interfaces with a and c (each angle is listed under (a, b, c) and (c, b, a));
  • compute_curvatures(): interface → its curvature in 1/pixel, unsigned: the length-weighted mean of the Menger curvature at its vertices, junctions excluded;
  • compute_area_faces(): material → its area in square pixels; the medium, label 0, comes out negative.

compute_lengths and compute_curvatures were wrong on most interfaces before 0.8.0 (the lengths by a median 7.4 %, migration): recompute anything derived from them with an earlier version.

docs.title: Files and the compressed segmentation
docs.text:
• algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh(filename, binary_mode=False) writes the mesh as a .rec file (text by default, as dw3d), always with a metadata appendix: dimension = 2, axis_order = yx, source_shape, the image-border vertices, the orientation rule (orientation = boundary_of_first_label) and, after construct_mesh_in_physical_units, the frame and the pixel size. dw2d.io.load_rec(filename) returns (points, segments, labels); dw2d.io.save_rec writes them; dw3d.io.rec_dimension(filename) tells a 2-D file from a 3-D one.
  • algorithm.last_compressed_segmentation is a dictionary (points, segments, labels, seeds, image_shape, image_border_vertices) from which dw2d.reconstruct_mask_from_dict(dictionary) rebuilds the mask; dw2d.save_compressed_segmentation(filename, dictionary) and dw2d.reconstruct_mask_from_saved_file_dict(filename) go through a file.

docs.title: Warnings
docs.text:
• UnresolvedCellWarning: a label of the mask absent from the mesh, named (also a mask whose mesh has no edge at all, which is returned empty); algorithm.unresolved_cells lists them.
  • EnclosedMediumWarning: a piece of label 0 that touches no side of the image; it is meshed as the outer medium (dw2d has no enclosed-medium region yet); algorithm.enclosed_medium_pockets lists them.
  • ThinMediumMarginWarning: a cell left with edges on a side of the image its pixels do not reach.

They are dw2d's own classes, distinct from dw3d's classes of the same names.

docs.title: Masks with anisotropic voxels (longer along z)
docs.text:
Most microscope stacks have a z step larger than their pixel size. Meshing such a mask on its own grid and scaling the mesh afterwards samples the surfaces coarsely along z, and every contact angle read from the mesh suffers. Resample the mask to cubic voxels first, by shape-based interpolation, and mesh in physical units:

algorithm = get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()
points, triangles, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing=(0.5, 0.3, 0.3), spacing_unit="um")
algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh("mesh.rec")   # records the frame and the source spacing in the appendix

The mesh comes out in the unit of spacing (do not call set_pixel_size on it); min_distance counts voxels of the resampled, cubic grid, so the mesh has as many points as for a mask acquired at the finer spacing, and costs as much: memory and time grow with the z/xy ratio. Measured on 12 simulated tissues of 90 and 165 cells voxelised at a real cell size and down-sampled along z (one seed), as the median over tissues of each mesh's median line-mean contact-angle error minus that of the same tissue meshed at full resolution: meshing the native grid costs +1.38, +1.97 and +4.10 degrees at ratios 5/3, 2 and 3; resampling first, +0.83, +0.71 and +1.17. These costs, and the quadric reading's below, were measured on 0.7.0's meshes, before 0.8.0 pads thin margins of medium on the native grid, and not measured again, because some of these runs need 8 to 40 GiB of memory. Nothing was measured above 3 at that cell size: above it the method warns (dw3d.UnmeasuredAnisotropyWarning) and still meshes. Keep foambryo's default (chord) reading: its quadric reading made every route worse at real cell size. The resampling alone is dw3d.resample_to_isotropic(mask, spacing). Repeating slices instead (method="nearest"), coarsening x and y to the z step, or telling only the distance transform about the spacing were all measured worse.

Example: the notebook Anisotropic voxels and crop faces (Examples/example_6_anisotropic_voxels_and_crop_faces.ipynb).

Scaling a mesh afterwards. set_pixel_size(xy_pixel_size, z_pixel_size) (the algorithm's method, the function in dw3d.mesh_utilities, and dw3d.set_points_pixel_size) scales column 0 of the points (the mask's axis 0, z) by z_pixel_size and columns 1 and 2 by xy_pixel_size. Before 0.7.0 it scaled columns 0 and 1 by the xy size and column 2 by the z size: re-run any analysis that called it with different sizes. A mask stored as (x, y, z) must be transposed to (z, y, x) first.

docs.title: Cropped tissues: crop faces and cut cells
docs.text:
When a cell of the mask reaches a face of the image box, the reconstruction closes it with triangles lying on that face. They are not contact with the medium: the tissue goes on beyond the image. The algorithm marks them as crop faces, and the cells they touch as cut cells, without changing the mesh:

points, triangles, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask)
algorithm.crop_faces          # boolean per triangle
algorithm.cut_cells           # labels of the cells the crop cuts
algorithm.crop_face_report.as_dict()   # counts per image face

foambryo keeps crop faces out of its equations and does not report the pressures of cut cells. A triangle the reconstruction puts on an image face that the mask's cell does not reach (the mask left a voxel or two of medium there) is not a crop face: it stays contact with the medium. If the tissue really ends on a face of the image (a coverslip), declare that face physical before reconstructing: its triangles then stay contact with the medium.

algorithm.physical_image_faces = ("axis0_low",)   # index 0 along the mask's first axis

The image faces are named "axis0_low", "axis0_high", ... "axis2_high" (dw3d.IMAGE_FACES). save_to_rec_mesh writes the crop faces as the last block of triangles and records them in the appendix below; dw3d.io.load_rec_with_crop_faces reads them back.

Example: the notebook Anisotropic voxels and crop faces (Examples/example_6_anisotropic_voxels_and_crop_faces.ipynb).

docs.title: A cell a few voxels from the image box
docs.text: A face of the image box that no cell reaches is not a crop: the medium goes on beyond it. Before 0.8.0 a cell a few voxels from such a face could take the medium between them (at min_distance 3 a 12-voxel cube 4 voxels from every face meshed to 2.98 times its voxel count). Since 0.8.0 such thin margins are padded with medium before meshing (masks of cubic voxels; a mask resampled from longer voxels is not padded unless asked), a face a cell reaches is never padded, and ThinMediumMarginWarning names a cell left on a face it does not reach; algorithm.medium_margin_padding says which faces were padded, and algorithm.pad_thin_medium_margins = False gives the previous meshes. On a padded face a cell's surface may pass the image box, by at most the padding. The rule, its measurements and its known issues, in 3D and in 2D: thin margins of medium.

docs.title: A cell the watershed loses (known issue)
docs.text:
The seeded watershed can lose a cell, most often a cell cut by the image box. A cell's seed is the tetrahedron whose centroid is nearest to the cell's deepest voxel. Against the image box this can be a thin tetrahedron whose faces all score below a face through which the rest of the cell, grouped without its seed, reaches a seeded neighbour; the neighbour then takes the whole group, the cell keeps only its seed, and mesh surgery relabels that tetrahedron. The cell is absent from the mesh, the neighbour comes out larger than its voxels, and cut_cells names the neighbour, which now holds the crop faces that were the lost cell's; crop_face_report.cells_reaching_a_crop_without_a_crop_face names the lost cell.

Since 0.8.0 such a cell is named: UnresolvedCellWarning lists it with the cause "removed by mesh surgery" (see Enclosed media, Regions too small for the mesh), and foambryo gives it no pressure. A smaller min_distance may mesh it. Measured on a test mask of four cells filling a ball that a 36³ image box cuts (cells 1, 3 and 4 have voxels on the box), at the default min_distance 3 on cubic voxels and without the padding of thin margins: cell 1 (1 648 voxels, 262 on the cut face) is absent from the mesh and cell 2 comes out at 1.37 times its voxels; at min_distance 1 and 2, and with z twice as long as x and y, every cell is meshed. On the same ball at 36 positions along z and min_distance 2 to 5, 16 cells are absent in 144 reconstructions; on 433 plane crops of the benchmark masks, cut_cells misses a cell on the box in 5, each lost or nearly lost by the watershed. With the padding of thin margins, the default, the ball's four faces that no cell reaches are padded and cell 1 is left only as a fragment of 4 triangles (0.010 of its voxel volume inside the box of voxel centres); the watershed's defect is unchanged, and pad_thin_medium_margins = False reproduces the loss above.

Compare a cut cell's mesh volume with its voxels inside the box of voxel centres, not with its voxel count: the mesh stops at the centres of the outermost voxels, so a cell cut by the box can reach at most about that volume (0.92 of the voxel count for cell 1 of the test mask above).

docs.title: Enclosed pockets of medium (lumens)
docs.text:
A mask's label 0 is the medium. A piece of label 0 that touches no face of the image is an enclosed pocket: a lumen, a cavity, or a hole in the segmentation. Before 0.7.1 such a pocket had no watershed seed (label 0 had a single one, at its deepest voxel, normally outside the tissue), so the first cell its tetrahedra reached took all of it. On a 697-cell embryo with a 389 918-voxel lumen, one lining cell came out at 2.40 times its voxel volume, and no lining cell kept a membrane against the lumen.

Since 0.7.1 a pocket becomes its own region, flagged as a medium, when both hold:

  • its inscribed radius (the largest distance, in voxels of the meshed grid, from one of its voxels to the nearest voxel outside it) is at least the point placement's min_distance + 1: 4 voxels at the default 3. A smaller pocket holds no tetrahedron of the tesselation, so it cannot be a region of the mesh;
  • two or more cells line it. A pocket inside a single cell is a hole in that cell's segmentation; as a region of its own its surface would have no triple line, and no method can infer the tension of such a surface.

The new labels are max + 1, max + 2, ..., in the order of each pocket's lowest raster index. Pieces are 6-connected (voxels sharing a face). Every other pocket stays with the cells, as before, and EnclosedMediumWarning names it with the cell that took it. Every piece of label 0 that touches the image box is exterior and gets its own seed.

from dw3d import get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm

algorithm = get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()
points, triangles, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(mask)
algorithm.medium_labels                     # (0, 774): the exterior and one enclosed medium
report = algorithm.enclosed_medium_report   # each medium's voxels, inscribed radius, lining cells
report.pockets_left_to_cells                # the pockets left to the cells, and which cell took each
algorithm.save_to_rec_mesh("mesh.rec")      # the appendix records "media = 0 774"

A medium is a region of the mesh like a cell: its interfaces with the cells are separate interfaces, so foambryo infers their tensions apart from those against the exterior, and the medium's own pressure. foambryo 0.7.1 reads the .rec file's media and reports and draws them as media, not cells (foambryo infer --media names them for a mesh made elsewhere). cell_volume_report leaves them out.

To reproduce 0.7.0's meshes, where every pocket goes to a cell, set algorithm.label_enclosed_media = False.

docs.title: Regions too small for the mesh
docs.text:
A region's watershed seed is the tetrahedron whose centroid is nearest to its deepest voxel. When no tetrahedron centroid lies in the region's voxels (a cell a few voxels across, or thinner than min_distance), that tetrahedron belongs to a neighbour; before 0.7.1 the region grew inside the neighbour as a phantom. Since 0.7.1 its seed is dropped: the region is absent from the mesh, UnresolvedCellWarning names it with its voxel count and the min_distance, enclosed_medium_report.unresolved lists it, and the .rec file records it (unresolved_regions). A smaller min_distance may mesh it.

Since 0.8.0 the reconstruction also checks the finished mesh against every label of the mask it meshed, so a region absent from the mesh for any reason is named, not only a region with no tetrahedron in its voxels. Each entry of enclosed_medium_report.unresolved (an UnresolvedRegion) says why, in cause: "no tetrahedron in its voxels" (the case above), "no watershed seed", "removed by mesh surgery" (the watershed left the region only its seed tetrahedron, and mesh surgery relabelled it; see A cell the watershed loses in Cropped tissues) or "no triangle in the mesh"; tetrahedra_after_the_watershed and tetrahedra_in_its_voxels give the counts behind it. UnresolvedCellWarning is emitted once, after the mesh is finished, naming every such region with its voxel count and its cause. The mesh itself does not change.

A mask whose mesh has no triangle at all (cells too small to hold a tetrahedron's centroid, such as cubes of side 1 to 4 voxels at min_distance 3, or a mask of label 0 only) is returned as an empty mesh, (0, 3) triangles and (0, 2) labels, with each cell named by UnresolvedCellWarning; before 0.8.0 it raised AxisError. save_to_rec_mesh writes the empty mesh, which load_rec reads back; save_to_vtk_mesh refuses it with a ValueError, as meshio cannot write such a file and read it back. dw2d does the same for a 2-D mask whose mesh has no edge.

On the benchmark, two cells are unresolved at every min_distance from 1 to 7: cell 2 of case 031 (62 voxels) and cell 7 of case 038 (26 voxels).

A mask with no pocket at or above the bound, one piece of exterior and every seed already inside its own region is reconstructed exactly as before: 45 of the 47 benchmark masks are.

docs.title: Straightening the junction lines (on by default since 0.5.0)
docs.text:
A reconstructed mesh's trijunction lines are ragged at voxel scale: the extraction places junction vertices wherever the tessellation happens to bracket them. Since 0.5.0 every reconstruction moves them onto the trijunction curves the mask itself gives, as a post-process on the finished mesh:

from dw3d import get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm

algorithm = get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()
points, triangles, labels = algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmentation_mask)
print(algorithm.relocation_provenance)          # did it run, with which guard, did it warn
print(algorithm.relocation_report.as_dict())    # what it moved

To reproduce the 0.4 meshes, switch it off: algorithm.relocate_junctions = False before reconstructing, or MeshReconstructionAlgorithmFactory().set_junction_relocation(False). At a point-placement min_distance of 5 or more the reconstruction emits dw3d.CoarseSpacingRelocationWarning once: the effect on surface-tangent contact angles there lies within the check's own noise and larger spacings are unmeasured; facet-based angles improve.

It can also be applied to a mesh you already have:

from dw3d import relocate_junction_vertices
from dw3d.io import load_rec

points, triangles, labels = load_rec("mesh.rec")
points, report = relocate_junction_vertices(segmentation_mask, points, triangles, labels)

It moves vertices and nothing else. Triangles and material labels come back untouched, so a treated mesh can be compared vertex-for-vertex with its own untreated original.

What it buys, measured over 40 benchmark cases at four reconstruction spacings and four point samplers: line position error, local tangent error and discrete curvature all improve at every spacing on every sampler, and no existing mesh-validity number changes on any case. If you are using a seed-free sampler (get_deterministic_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm) it also improves contact angles by 2.3–3.5 degrees and downstream tension error by 20–40 %, and brings the junction lines to the default sampler's own untreated accuracy or better. On the default's seeded sampler the lines improve and the contact angles do not move significantly. See BENCHMARKS.md (measured before relocation became the default).

What it costs: about +0.75 s on the benchmark meshes, whose reconstruction takes about 5 s (+15 %); 0.1–1.5 s per timepoint on real embryo volumes, whose reconstruction takes about 0.6 s (median 0.34 s and 0.48 s on two time series). Within one real series it grows faster than linearly with mesh size (fitted exponent 2.68 over a 2.2-fold range — not a tissue-scale law). Since 0.6.0 the guard finds its candidate vertex pairs with a batched neighbour search, which leaves every relocated mesh bit-for-bit unchanged: on a 1 866-cell tissue the guard takes 45 s instead of 6.6 min.

It cannot make the mesh pass through itself. Every accepted move is checked against the whole mesh, not only the triangles around the vertex it moves, so the number of self-intersecting triangle pairs can never rise. That check is available on its own as dw3d.count_self_intersections(points, triangles).

Example: the notebook Default junction relocation (Examples/example_5_default_junction_relocation.ipynb).

docs.title: Orientation of the meshes in 2D and 3D
docs.text: Both packages store, with every mesh element, the two regions it separates, smaller label first, and orient the element by one rule. foambryo reads that rule to know which region is on which side of an interface, which is what the sign of a pressure difference depends on. This page states the rule once, for triangles and for edges, with the test that decides it.

docs.title: The rule
docs.text:
Notation: a mask's index frame is the order of its axes, \((i, j, k) = (z, y, x)\) for a 3-D stack (columns 0, 1, 2 of points) and \((\text{row}, \text{column})\) for a 2-D image (columns 0, 1). Both frames are taken right-handed in that order. labels[n] = (a, b) with \(a < b\).

Each mesh element is the positively oriented boundary of its first label \(a\), in the index frame.

  • Triangles (dw3d), vertices \(p_0, p_1, p_2\) in \((i, j, k)\): the right-hand normal $$ \mathbf{n} = (p_1 - p_0) \times (p_2 - p_0) $$ points out of \(a\) and into \(b\).
  • Edges (dw2d), vertices \(p_0 \to p_1\) in \((\text{row}, \text{column})\), tangent \(\mathbf{t} = p_1 - p_0 = (\Delta r, \Delta c)\): material \(a\) lies on the left of \(\mathbf{t}\), so the normal $$ \mathbf{n} = (\Delta c, -\Delta r), $$ the tangent turned clockwise, points out of \(a\) and into \(b\).

"Positively oriented boundary" is Stokes' convention, outward normal first: a triangle is positively oriented as boundary of a region \(R\) when \(\det(\mathbf{n}_\text{out}, p_1 - p_0, p_2 - p_0) > 0\), i.e. when its right-hand normal points out of \(R\); an edge when \(\det(\mathbf{n}_\text{out}, \mathbf{t}) > 0\), i.e. when \(R\) lies on the left of \(\mathbf{t}\). Equivalently, each material's elements, taken as stored where it is \(a\) and reversed where it is \(b\), run counter-clockwise around it: seen from outside in 3D, in the \((\text{row}, \text{column})\) plane in 2D.

docs.title: The test that decides it: signed volume and signed area
docs.text:
Take one cell (label 1) alone in the medium (label 0): every element carries \((a, b) = (0, 1)\) and is, by the rule, the positive boundary of the medium. By the divergence theorem, the signed volume and the signed area of the stored elements,

\[ V = \frac{1}{6} \sum_n \det(p_0, p_1, p_2), \qquad A = \frac{1}{2} \sum_n \left( p_{0,\text{row}}\, p_{1,\text{column}} - p_{0,\text{column}}\, p_{1,\text{row}} \right), \]

are minus the enclosed measure: \(V < 0\) and \(A < 0\) (they would be positive if the elements were the cell's boundary, i.e. under the opposite rule). Measured on a ball of radius 9 voxels (dw3d's default algorithm, a 28-voxel cube) and a disk of radius 20 pixels (dw2d's, a 60-pixel square): \(V = -2407\) cubic voxels (3112 voxels in the ball; every right-hand normal points to the centre, into the cell) and \(A = -1244\) square pixels (1264 pixels in the disk; the normal \((\Delta c, -\Delta r)\) points into the cell on every edge). tests/test_orientation_of_two_and_three_dimensional_meshes.py pins both signs, on every route that returns a 2-D mesh (the algorithm, the half-edge structure, the compressed segmentation, the .rec file, dw3d's object given a 2-D mask).

The same test, cell by cell, tells the rule of any 2-D mesh: the signed area of a cell's boundary, each edge counted as stored where the cell is \(a\) and reversed where it is \(b\), is positive for every cell under the rule. foambryo measures it this way on every 2-D mesh it reads.

docs.title: Before 0.8.0
docs.text:
dw2d stored every edge the other way round until 0.8.0: \(a\) lay on the right of \(p_0 \to p_1\) in \((\text{row}, \text{column})\) (on its left in \((x, y) = (\text{column}, \text{row})\), the frame of dw2d's former docstrings), so each edge was the boundary of its second label, the opposite of dw3d's rule in index order, and the disk above had \(A = +1244\). Since 0.8.0 the two vertices of each edge are swapped; no vertex, edge, label or edge order changes, and dw2d's half-edge quantities (angles, lengths, curvatures, cell areas) are bitwise those of before. dw3d's triangles do not change.

A 2-D .rec file written by dw2d's algorithm since 0.8.0 records the rule in its appendix, orientation = boundary_of_first_label (dw2d.io.ORIENTATION_RECORDED). Files written before carry no such key. foambryo does not rely on the key: it measures each 2-D mesh's orientation from its geometry, reverses a mesh in the former orientation (so the tensions and pressures are the same from either), and refuses a mesh whose cells disagree, or whose geometry contradicts the rule its file records.

docs.title: The .rec / .arec metadata appendix
docs.text:
save_rec/load_rec (dw3d.io) read and write .rec/.arec multimaterial mesh files (points, triangles, and per-triangle material labels; text or binary). The text layout is the point count, one x y z line per point, the triangle count, and one v0 v1 v2 label1 label2 line per triangle. Since 0.8.0 the files are read and written by iorec (iorec>=1.4.1), with the same names and signatures in dw3d.io, and the same arrays and typed appendix values as before. The binary layout (binary_mode=True), little-endian on every machine, is the point count (uint64), the points (3 float64 each), the triangle count (uint64), then per triangle its 3 vertex indices (int64) and its 2 labels (int32). The points are always written as float64, whatever their dtype in memory, so a file reads back the same. Optionally, a .rec/.arec file can carry a small metadata appendix: pass metadata={...} to save_rec, and read it back with load_rec_appendix(filename).

The appendix is a trailing block of ASCII # key = value lines, written after the geometry data — never before it, because every existing reader (this one included) reads a count and then exactly that many values, so a trailing block is invisible to them, while a leading one breaks parsing outright. Fields:

# rec-appendix 1
# written_by = dw3d <version>
# writer_library = iorec <version>
# dimension = 3
# coordinate_frame = voxel_index
# axis_order = zyx
# spacing = 1.0 0.325 0.325
# spacing_unit = um
# source_shape = 194 200 199
# crop_offset = 0 0 0
  • coordinate_frame is voxel_index, physical, or unknown — this is the field the appendix exists for, since spacing alone can't tell a reader whether coordinates are raw voxel indices awaiting a scale or physical units that already have it applied.
  • axis_order, spacing/spacing_unit, source_shape and crop_offset record the rest of the sampling geometry, crop_offset even when zero (where the mask sat in a larger image; the crop faces themselves are recorded by crop_faces, below).
  • A file with no appendix must be treated as coordinate_frame == "unknown", never as isotropic spacing — load_rec_appendix returns None in that case, and every file saved before this feature existed has no appendix.
  • crop_faces = <first row> <count> says that the last <count> triangle rows, from <first row> on, are crop faces (see Cropped tissues), and physical_image_faces which image faces were declared physical (none by default). Written by save_to_rec_mesh whenever a cell of the mask reaches the image box where the mesh lies on it; a file without the key records nothing about a crop.
  • media = 0 L ... lists the labels that are media, not cells: the exterior 0, then the enclosed pockets of medium the reconstruction made their own regions (see Enclosed pockets of medium), with enclosed_media_voxels and enclosed_media_inscribed_radius aligned with the enclosed labels. Written only when the mesh has an enclosed medium; a file without the key has the exterior 0 as its only medium.
  • unresolved_regions = L ... and unresolved_regions_voxels list the labels of the mask absent from the mesh, whatever the cause (see Enclosed pockets of medium), with their voxel counts; before 0.8.0 only those with no tetrahedron of the tesselation in their voxels. Written only when there is one.
  • construct_mesh_in_physical_units writes coordinate_frame = physical, the mask's own spacing (the mesh is already scaled by it), source_shape, resampling and resampled_spacing (see Masks with anisotropic voxels).
  • dimension is 3 for dw3d's meshes and 2 for dw2d's. dw3d.io.rec_dimension(filename) reads it, or, for a file without it, tells the dimension from the file's layout (the coordinates per point row of a text file; which binary layout accounts exactly for the geometry's bytes), and refuses a file it cannot classify; dw3d.io.load_rec refuses a 2-D file and names dw2d.io.load_rec. dw3d writes dimension whenever it writes an appendix; a file without one is written byte for byte as before. dw2d's save_to_rec_mesh (and dw3d's, given a 2-D mask) always writes an appendix, with dimension = 2, axis_order = yx, source_shape, the image-border vertices and orientation = boundary_of_first_label, the rule its edges follow (orientation); dw2d.io.save_rec writes one only when given metadata, and the deprecated export_mesh writes none.
  • writer_library names the iorec version that wrote the file; written_by names dw3d's (or dw2d's) version.

The appendix written is version 1 (# key = value lines), on purpose. iorec also reads and writes a version 2 (# key: <JSON> lines), and delaunay-watershed 0.8.0 reads it, typing its values by their JSON. It does not write it: delaunay-watershed-3d 0.7.1 and foambryo 0.7.1 read a version-2 block without any error but lose every key of it (crop faces, media, unresolved regions, spacing), while they read every key of version 1. dw3d.io.APPENDIX_VERSION_WRITTEN is 1.

docs.title: Reconstruction variants
docs.text:
get_default_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm gives you the default reconstruction: the published algorithm (equivalent to dw3d 0.3.6). It is the more accurate one for downstream tension inference today, so it is what most users should start with.

A revised meshing pipeline is also available, opt-in, as get_link_checked_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm. It is deterministic, protects triple junctions explicitly, and produces cleaner topology and lower interface-area bias than the default — but as measured on foambryo's benchmarking dataset, meshes it produces currently give worse end-to-end tension-inference accuracy than the default, on every inference method tested (see BENCHMARKS.md). Reach for it when mesh geometry and topology matter more to you than today's downstream inference accuracy — for example, when the mesh itself, rather than inferred tensions, is the deliverable:

from dw3d import get_link_checked_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm

mesh_reconstruction_algorithm = get_link_checked_mesh_reconstruction_algorithm()
mesh_reconstruction_algorithm.construct_mesh_from_segmentation_mask(segmentation_mask)

docs.title: Thin margins of medium
docs.text: A face of the image box (a side of the image, in 2D) that no cell reaches is not a crop: the medium goes on beyond it. Before 0.8.0, a cell a few voxels from such a face could take the medium between them. Since 0.8.0 thin margins are padded with medium before meshing, in both packages, with one rule.

docs.title: The defect
docs.text: The distance field the points are placed on is 0 on the image box's outer voxels, below the membranes (0.73 on a flat membrane), and a point is placed only where no lower value lies within min_distance. So the membrane facing a nearby face of the box lost its points to the box (at a margin of 2 or 3 voxels it had none at all, at min_distance 3), the tetrahedra joining the cell to the box spanned the medium, and the watershed gave them to the cell. Measured before 0.8.0 at min_distance 3: a 12-voxel cube 4 voxels from every face meshed to 2.98 times its voxel count, and the two boxes of a 24-voxel test mask to 2.46 and 2.44 times; the range of margins affected grows with min_distance (up to margins of 5–7 voxels at min_distance 3, 7–8 at 4, 8–10 at 5). In 2D, at min_distance 4, a 20-pixel square 2, 3 or 4 pixels from every side meshed to 1.25, 1.37 and 1.28 times its pixels, and a 12-pixel square 3 or 4 pixels from one side collapsed to a triangle of 0.23 times its pixels at min_distance 5.

docs.title: The padding
docs.text:
Every face that no cell reaches and whose margin (its smallest gap to a cell) is below 2 * min_distance + 2 voxels or pixels is padded with label 0 up to that bound; the mesh is built on the padded mask and returned in the mask's frame.

  • pad_thin_medium_margins (attribute or constructor argument of the algorithm, in dw3d and dw2d): True by default since 0.8.0; False gives the meshes of earlier versions.
  • algorithm.medium_margin_padding: which faces were padded, and by how many voxels or pixels.
  • A face that a cell reaches is a crop: it is never padded, and no vertex passes it.
  • ThinMediumMarginWarning: a cell left with triangles (edges, in 2D) on a face its voxels do not reach, named with the face and its margin.
  • On a padded face the cell is meshed as if it had been imaged with a wider margin, so its surface may reach a few voxels into the medium there, and past the image box when the margin is thinner than the padding: by at most the face's padding. Measured: up to 7 voxels on a 16-voxel cube 1 voxel from every face, 1 to 4 voxels on foambryo's test masks, 0 to 2 voxels on the lab's data.

In 3D the padding is decided from a first mesh: the mask is padded when that mesh has a vertex on a face no cell reaches, and is then meshed again. The mask's own voxels keep the random dither of the point placement they have unpadded, so the mesh changes only within the padded faces' reach. Measured on cubes of side 12 to 24 voxels at margins of 2 to 5 voxels, the volume ratio is now 0.75–1.09 (the 12-voxel cube 4 voxels from every face: 1.09; the test mask's two boxes 1.01 and 0.81). Of the lab's 684 test masks (the 47 benchmark masks, the 141 masks of the resolution sweep, 492 frames of two real embryo series and four test images), 18 change, and the others are meshed bit for bit as before, among them every benchmark mask; the benchmarks say what the change does to the 13 sweep masks it affects.

In 2D dw2d places its points without a dither, so it decides from the mask before meshing, with one run. On squares, squares near one side, a doublet and disks at min_distance 3, 4 and 5, every cell at a margin of 1 to 10 pixels now meshes to 0.84–0.99 times its pixels (0.23–1.73 before). None of the repository's 2-D masks is padded (the smallest margin of a side no cell reaches is 12 pixels), so their meshes are unchanged. dw3d's algorithm passes its pad_thin_medium_margins to dw2d for a 2-D mask.

docs.title: Masks resampled from longer voxels are not padded by default
docs.text: construct_mesh_in_physical_units resamples a mask whose voxels are longer along one axis to cubic voxels. It does not pad such a mask unless asked for that call (construct_mesh_in_physical_units(mask, spacing, pad_thin_medium_margins=True)); a mask of cubic voxels is padded on both routes. Reason, measured on a test mask of four cells filling a ball 4 voxels from the image box, with z twice as long as x and y, over 100 seeds of the point placement's dither: a cell kept less than half its voxel volume on 20 of 100 seeds with the padding (95 % interval 0.13–0.29) against 3 of 100 without it (0.006–0.085; McNemar exact p = 1.5e-5); with cubic voxels, 13 against 10 (p = 0.51). The cell is lost in the watershed, not at its seed nor in mesh surgery; why this happens more often on resampled masks was not found. Unpadded, a resampled mask keeps the 0.7 meshes near thin margins, with their defect (on the same ball with x 2.5 times as long, one cell comes out at 7.47 times its voxel volume unpadded, 0.78 padded), and ThinMediumMarginWarning names each cell that lies on a face it does not reach.

docs.title: Known issues
docs.text:
• Resampled masks: above; the padding is off there by default because it made the watershed lose cells more often (20 of 100 seeds against 3 of 100).
  • In 3D, a cell that collapses without reaching the box is not padded. The decision is taken from the first mesh's vertices, so a small cell that collapses near a face without a vertex on it is missed: on cubes of side 6 to 12 voxels at 1 to 5 voxels from one face or from every face, at min_distance 3 to 5 and 10 dither seeds (1 200 reconstructions), 25 cubes collapsed to 0.00–0.49 of their voxels with no vertex on a face of the box, so the mask was not padded; padded, the same masks give 0.58–0.80. dw2d decides from the mask and has no such blind spot; the two packages therefore decide differently in this release.
  • The surface can pass the image box on a padded face, by at most the padding (above).
  • An 8-voxel cube no longer exceeds 1.5 times its voxels, though it can fall to 0.10, as it does on 2 of 20 dither seeds 8 voxels from every face without any padding.

API: dw3d.thin_medium_margins, dw2d.thin_medium_margins.
